readmeText:
OpenCodeReview

 English | 简体中文 | 日本語 | 한국어 | Русский

 What is Open Code Review?

 Open Code Review is an AI-powered code review CLI tool. It originated as Alibaba Group's internal official AI code review assistant — over the past two years, it has served tens of thousands of developers and identified millions of code defects. After thorough validation at massive scale, we incubated it into an open source project for the community. Simply configure a model endpoint to get started.

 It reads Git diffs, sends changed files to a configurable LLM via an agent with tool-use capabilities, and generates structured review comments with line-level precision. The agent can read full file contents, search the codebase, inspect other changed files for context, and produce deep reviews — not just surface-level diff feedback. Beyond diff review, ocr scan reviews entire files for auditing unfamiliar codebases or directories that have no meaningful diff.

 Visit the official website for more details.

 Benchmark

 Compared to general-purpose agents (Claude Code), Open Code Review achieves significantly higher Precision and F1 with the same underlying model, while consuming only ~1/9 of the tokens and completing reviews faster. Note that its Recall is lower than general-purpose agents — a deliberate trade-off favoring precision over noise.

 A real-world code review benchmark built from 50 popular open-source repositories, 200 real Pull Requests, and 10 programming languages — cross-validated by 80+ senior engineers ( 1,505 annotated ground-truth issues).

 Explore the AACR-Bench dataset on Hugging Face .

 Metric
 What it measures
 Why it matters

 F1
 Harmonic mean of precision and recall
 Best single number for overall review quality

 Precision
 Proportion of reported issues that are real defects
 Higher = fewer false alarms to triage

 Recall
 Proportion of real defects that are found
 Higher = fewer issues slip through review

 Avg Time
 Wall-clock time per review
 Matters for CI pipeline latency

 Avg Token
 Total tokens consumed per review
 Directly impacts API cost

 Why Open Code Review?

 The Problem with General-Purpose Agents

 If you've used general-purpose agents like Claude Code with Skills for code review, you've likely encountered these pain points:

- Incomplete coverage — On larger changesets, agents tend to "cut corners," selectively reviewing only some files and missing others.

- Position drift — Reported issues frequently don't match the actual code location, with line numbers or file references drifting off target.

- Unstable quality — Natural-language-driven Skills are hard to debug, and review quality fluctuates significantly with minor prompt variations.

 The root cause: a purely language-driven architecture lacks hard constraints on the review process.

 Core Design: Deterministic Engineering × Agent Hybrid

 Open Code Review's core philosophy is to combine deterministic engineering with an agent, each handling what it does best.

 Deterministic Engineering — Hard Constraints

 For review steps that must not go wrong , engineering logic — not the language model — guarantees correctness:

- Precise file selection — Determines exactly which files need review and which should be filtered, ensuring no important change is missed.

- Smart file bundling — Groups related files into a single review unit (e.g., message_en.properties and message_zh.properties are bundled together). Each bundle runs as a sub-agent with isolated context — a divide-and-conquer strategy that stays stable on very large changesets and naturally supports concurrent review.

- Fine-grained rule matching — Matches review rules to each file's characteristics, keeping the model's attention sharply focused and eliminating information noise at the source. Compared to purely language-driven rule guidance, template-engine-based rule matching is more stable and predictable.

- External positioning and reflection modules — Independent comment-positioning and comment-reflection modules systematically improve both the location accuracy and content accuracy of AI feedback.

 Agent — Dynamic Decision-Making

 The agent's strengths are concentrated where they matter most — dynamic decisions and dynamic context retrieval:

- Scenario-tuned prompts — Prompt templates deeply optimized for code review, improving effectiveness while reducing token consumption.

- Scenario-tuned toolset — Distilled from deep analysis of tool-call traces in large-scale production data — including call frequency distributions, per-tool repetition rates, and the impact of new tools on the overall call chain — resulting in a purpose-built toolset that is more stable and predictable for code review than a generic agent toolkit.

 How to Use

 Prerequisites

- Git >= 2.41 — Open Code Review relies on Git for diff generation, code search, and repository operations.

 Agent Skills

 Use the skills in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kimi Code, or another agent that supports Agent Skills and can run local commands. Both modes require Git >= 2.41 and the ocr CLI ; only native mode requires an OCR model provider.

 1. Install the Skills

 Run in the project you want to review, then select the skills you need and your agent in the installer:

 npx skills add alibaba/open-code-review

 The skills guide your agent to install ocr if it is missing, subject to your environment's permissions. You can also install it ahead of time with npm install -g @alibaba-group/open-code-review . Prefer a plugin or manual installation? See the agent-specific setup guide , or copy the desired folders from skills/ into your agent's skill directory.

 2. Choose a Review Mode

 Native mode
 Delegation mode

 Skill
 open-code-review
 open-code-review-delegate

 Who reviews?
 OCR's specialized review agent and pipeline
 Your current coding agent, following OCR's review pipeline and guardrails

 Model and authentication
 OCR's own provider configuration
 Your host agent's existing model and authentication

 Choose it when
 You have a model endpoint for OCR and want its full review pipeline
 You have no separate API key, or want to use your existing agent subscription/setup

 No separate key? Start with delegation mode. It skips OCR provider setup, not the host agent's own authentication, usage limits, or costs. A host-agent subscription is not automatically an API credential for native mode. In delegation mode, OCR's CLI and skill together provide the review pipeline and guardrails: file selection, rule resolution, coverage requirements, and structured reporting. The host agent performs analysis, positioning, and reporting within that workflow; it does not run OCR's full native pipeline.

 For native mode, configure a provider once with ocr config provider and ocr config model . Authentication depends on the provider; see Configuration .

 CLI

 Install

 npm install -g @alibaba-group/open-code-review

 After installation, the ocr command is available globally.

 For other installation methods (install script, GitHub Release binary, from source), see Installation .

 Quick Start

 1. Configure LLM

 You must configure an LLM before reviewing code, unless you use Delegation Mode .

- OCR calls the model: ocr review , the /open-code-review:review command, and the open-code-review skill use OCR's own provider configuration, not your Claude Code Team/Pro subscription login. Authentication requirements depend on the provider; see Configuration .

- The host agent calls the model: the /open-code-review:delegate-review command and the open-code-review-delegate skill use the host agent's configured model and authentication. No separate LLM configuration or credentials are needed in OCR. See the Claude Code install steps .

 ocr config provider # Select a built-in provider or add a custom one
ocr config model # Pick a model for the active provider

 The interactive UI guides you through provider selection, API key entry, and model configuration, then automatically tests connectivity.

 For CLI setup, environment variables, custom providers, and other advanced configuration, see Configuration .

 2. Review

 cd your-project

 # Workspace mode — review all staged, unstaged, and untracked changes
ocr review

 # Current branch — review changes since it diverged from main (--to defaults to HEAD)
ocr review --from main

 # Branch range — reviews feature-branch's changes since it diverged from main (merge-base mode)
ocr review --from main --to feature-branch

 # Single commit
ocr review --commit abc123

 # Resume an interrupted range or commit review
ocr session list
ocr review --from main --to feature-branch --resume < session-id >

 # Full-file scan — review whole files instead of a diff (no git history needed)
ocr scan # scan the entire repository
ocr scan --path internal/agent # scan a directory or specific files
ocr scan --resume < session-id > # resume an interrupted full-file scan

 # Save results to a file (recommended for AI host agents)
ocr review --format json --output result.json

 # Delegation mode — let your AI coding agent perform the review itself
 # OCR handles file selection and rule resolution; no LLM configuration needed
ocr delegate preview
ocr delegate rule src/main.go src/handler.go

 Documentation

 Full documentation lives at open-codereview.ai/docs :

- Quickstart — install and run your first review

- Installation — all platforms and package managers

- CLI Reference — every command and flag

- Review Rules — customize review rules with path filtering and targeting

- Configuration — config keys and environment variables

- MCP Server — extend the review agent with external tools

- Coding Agent Integrations — choose the platform you use

- Claude Code — install a plugin with review slash commands

- Codex — install a plugin with callable review skills

- Cursor — install a plugin with portable review skills

- Kimi Code — install a plugin with review slash commands and skills

- OpenCode — install native review tools and slash commands

- QCA Forward — run delegation mode with the QCA host model and a ready-to-publish template

- Skill-compatible agents — install the portable agent skill

- Review Execution Modes — after integration, choose which LLM performs the review

- Default (OCR-managed) — OCR runs the review using its configured LLM

- Delegation Mode — your coding agent runs the review using its own LLM; no OCR API key required

- CI/CD Integration — GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, GitFlic CI, and Gerrit integration

- Session Viewer — browse and replay review sessions in browser, mark comments as fixed or ignored and hide them while you work through the findings

- Telemetry — OpenTelemetry integration for observability

- FAQ — common questions and troubleshooting

 Contributing

 This project exists thanks to all the people who contribute. See CONTRIBUTING.md for development setup, coding guidelines, and how to submit pull requests.

 License

 Apache-2.0 — Copyright 2026 Alibaba

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Superpowers

 Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

 Table of Contents

- How it works

- Commercial Services

- Getting Started

- Claude Code

- Antigravity

- Codex App

- Codex CLI

- Cursor

- Devin CLI

- Factory Droid

- Gemini CLI

- GitHub Copilot CLI

- Grok Build CLI

- Kimi Code

- OpenCode

- Pi

- Qwen Code

- Hermes Agent

- Muse

- The Basic Workflow

- When Something Goes Wrong

- Community

- What's Inside

- Philosophy

- Contributing

- Updating

- License

- Visual companion telemetry

 How it works

 It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it doesn't just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do.

 Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest.

 After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY.

 Next up, once you say "go", it launches a subagent-driven-development process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

 There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

 Commercial Services

 If you're using Superpowers in enterprise and could benefit from commercial support, additional tooling, or managed spending, please don't hesitate to drop us a line at sales@primeradiant.com .

 Installation

 Installation differs by harness. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one.

 Claude Code

 Superpowers is available via the official Claude plugin marketplace

 Official Marketplace

-
 Install the plugin from Anthropic's official marketplace:

 /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official

 Superpowers Marketplace

 The Superpowers marketplace provides Superpowers and some other related plugins for Claude Code.

-
 Register the marketplace:

 /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace

-
 Install the plugin from this marketplace:

 /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

 Antigravity

 Install Superpowers as a plugin from this repository:

 agy plugin install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

 Antigravity lists each installed skill's description, and the description of
the using-superpowers skill prompts the model to load that skill at the start
of a conversation. Reinstall with the same command to update.

 Codex App

 Superpowers is available via the official Codex plugin marketplace .

- In the Codex app, click on Plugins in the sidebar.

- You should see Superpowers in the Coding section.

- Click the + next to Superpowers and follow the prompts.

 Codex CLI

 Superpowers is available via the official Codex plugin marketplace .

-
 Open the plugin search interface:

 /plugins

-
 Search for Superpowers:

 superpowers

-
 Select Install Plugin .

 Cursor

-
 In Cursor Agent chat, install from marketplace:

 /add-plugin superpowers

-
 Or search for "superpowers" in the plugin marketplace.

 Devin CLI

-
 Install the plugin from this repository:

 devin plugins install obra/superpowers

-
 Update to the latest version with:

 devin plugins update superpowers

 Factory Droid

-
 Register the marketplace:

 droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Install the plugin:

 droid plugin install superpowers@superpowers

 Gemini CLI

-
 Install the extension:

 gemini extensions install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Update later:

 gemini extensions update superpowers

 GitHub Copilot CLI

-
 Register the marketplace:

 copilot plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace

-
 Install the plugin:

 copilot plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

 Grok Build CLI

 Superpowers is available via the official Grok plugin marketplace .

-
 Install the plugin from xAI's official marketplace:

 grok plugin install superpowers@xai-official --trust

-
 Or open the marketplace in the TUI, search for Superpowers, and install it:

 /marketplace

 Kimi Code

 Superpowers is available in Kimi Code's plugin marketplace.

-
 Open Kimi Code's plugin manager:

 /plugins

-
 Go to Marketplace > Superpowers and install it.

-
 Or install directly from this repository:

 /plugins install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Detailed docs: docs/README.kimi.md

 OpenCode

 OpenCode uses its own plugin install; install Superpowers separately even if you
already use it in another harness.

-
 Tell OpenCode:

 Fetch and follow instructions from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obra/superpowers/refs/heads/main/.opencode/INSTALL.md

-
 Detailed docs: docs/README.opencode.md

 Pi

 Install Superpowers as a Pi package from this repository:

 pi install git:github.com/obra/superpowers

 For local development, run Pi with this checkout loaded as a temporary package:

 pi -e /path/to/superpowers

 The Pi package loads the Superpowers skills and a small extension that injects the using-superpowers bootstrap at session startup and again after compaction. Pi has native skills, so no compatibility Skill tool is required. Subagent and task-list tools remain optional Pi companion packages.

 Qwen Code

 Qwen Code installs plugins from Claude Code marketplaces directly.

-
 Install the plugin from this repository, and pick superpowers when prompted:

 qwen extensions install obra/superpowers

-
 Update later:

 qwen extensions update superpowers

 Hermes Agent

 Install Superpowers as a Hermes plugin from this repository:

 hermes plugins install obra/superpowers --enable

 Restart any active Hermes sessions after installing. Note: Hermes has no
post-compaction hook, so a very long session that compacts over its first
turn loses the bootstrap — start a fresh session if skills stop triggering.

 Muse

 Superpowers is available as a native Muse plugin — same repo, same skills, all harnesses. The using-superpowers bootstrap is injected via the native SessionStart hook alongside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Pi, and the rest — no per-session opt-in.

-
 Install from a local checkout:

 muse plugins install ./
muse plugins approve superpowers

 Or clone and install:

 git clone https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git
muse plugins install ./superpowers
muse plugins approve superpowers

-
 Update later:

 muse plugins update superpowers

 Restart any active Muse sessions after installing so the SessionStart hook takes effect — skills are active immediately, hooks require approval on first install. To verify, start a fresh session and send Let's make a react todo list — a working install auto-triggers brainstorming before any code is written. Version is tracked in .version-bump.json so scripts/bump-version.sh keeps it in sync.

 The Basic Workflow

-
 brainstorming - Activates before building anything. Draws out what you actually want, and why, through questions that get you describing it, then plays its understanding back for correction. Small changes get agreed in chat; projects get a written design document a builder could plan from.

-
 using-git-worktrees - Activates after design approval. Creates isolated workspace on new branch, runs project setup, verifies clean test baseline.

-
 writing-plans - Activates with approved design. Breaks work into bite-sized tasks (2-5 minutes each). Every task has exact file paths, complete code, verification steps.

-
 subagent-driven-development or executing-plans - Activates with plan. Either dispatches a fresh subagent per task with a review after each (most thorough), or implements every task inline in the current session with one fresh review of the whole branch at the end (cheapest).

-
 test-driven-development - Activates during implementation. Enforces RED-GREEN-REFACTOR: write failing test, watch it fail, write minimal code, watch it pass, commit. Deletes code written before tests.

-
 requesting-code-review - Activates between tasks. Reviews against plan, reports issues by severity. Critical issues block progress.

-
 finishing-a-development-branch - Activates when tasks complete. Verifies tests, presents options (merge/PR/keep/discard), cleans up worktree.

 The agent checks for relevant skills before any task. Mandatory workflows, not suggestions.

 When Something Goes Wrong

 Sometimes a session misbehaves: a skill fires when it shouldn't, stays silent when it should, or the agent ignores its plan, repeats work, or burns more tokens than you'd expect. Ask your coding agent to "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in this session" and it will invoke the diagnosing-superpowers skill. To examine an earlier session, name it: "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in session <id> ".

 The skill reads the session transcript, reports what happened with line-level evidence, and, if you want, packages a scrubbed bundle for a bug report.

 Community

 Superpowers is built by Jesse Vincent and the rest of the folks at Prime Radiant .

- Discord : Join us for community support, questions, and sharing what you're building with Superpowers

- Issues : https://github.com/obra/superpowers/issues

- Release announcements : Sign up to get notified about new versions

 What's Inside

 Skills Library

 Testing

- test-driven-development - RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle (includes testing anti-patterns reference)

 Debugging

- systematic-debugging - 4-phase root cause process (includes root-cause-tracing, defense-in-depth, condition-based-waiting techniques)

- verification-before-completion - Ensure it's actually fixed

- diagnosing-superpowers - Work out what went wrong in a session, with evidence; export a scrubbed bundle or file an issue

 Collaboration

- brainstorming - Drawing out intent before building

- writing-plans - Detailed implementation plans

- executing-plans - Inline plan execution: one context, one final review

- dispatching-parallel-agents - Concurrent subagent workflows

- requesting-code-review - Pre-review checklist

- receiving-code-review - Responding to feedback

- using-git-worktrees - Parallel development branches

- finishing-a-development-branch - Merge/PR decision workflow

- subagent-driven-development - Fast iteration with two-stage review (spec compliance, then code quality)

 Meta

- writing-skills - Create new skills following best practices (includes testing methodology)

- using-superpowers - Introduction to the skills system

 Philosophy

- Test-Driven Development - Write tests first, always

- Systematic over ad-hoc - Process over guessing

- Complexity reduction - Simplicity as primary goal

- Evidence over claims - Verify before declaring success

 Read the original release announcement .

 Contributing

 The general contribution process for Superpowers is below. Keep in mind that we don't generally accept contributions of new skills and that any updates to skills must work across all of the coding agents we support. We also don't accept agent-written PRs that fix issues filed by someone else unless a maintainer asked for one, even when you hit the same problem; add your report to the existing issue instead.

- Fork the repository

- Switch to the 'dev' branch

- Create a branch for your work

- Follow the writing-skills skill for creating and testing new and modified skills

- Submit a PR, filling in every section of the pull request template, including the sum...

Build your own AI office with Univer Office SDK.

 Start with open-source Sheets and Docs, then connect your own application or agent.

 🚀 Quick start · 💼 Workspace · 📚 Documentation · ⚖️ Feature comparison · 🌐 Website · 🎮 Showcase · 🔧 API Reference · 📝 Blog

 English · Français · Deutsch · Español · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어

 Table of contents

- 💡 What is Univer?

- Open-source capabilities

- 🚀 Build on the open-source foundation

- Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor

- Connect your application to editable content

- 🏗️ Explore the open-source architecture

- Give custom features clear boundaries

- Compose cross-feature edits and undo/redo

- Connect applications and agents through Facade APIs and events

- 🧩 Extend your application with Univer Office SDK

- Scope and licensing

- 🌐 Application patterns and ecosystem

- Univer Workspace: an Office SDK reference application

- CLI, agent integrations, and developer skills

- 📚 Documentation and contributing

- Runtime compatibility

- 💬 Community

- 🔒 Security

- ❤️ Sponsors

- 📄 License

 💡 What is Univer?

 Univer is an Office SDK for building Office applications inside your own product. It provides Office editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing for people and existing agents, using your data and permissions. The product family covers spreadsheets, documents, presentations, relational tables, canvases, and PDFs.

 Univer Office SDK has three parts:

- Web SDK is the foundation: content models, editing, rendering, formula calculation, and Facade APIs (application-facing APIs). Compose its plugins into an embedded editor or your own Office application, and reuse the content models, commands, and calculation for Headless processing without an interactive editor.

- Server SDK adds backend services for real-time collaboration, edit history, and Office file import and export.

- AI SDK connects Office capabilities to existing agents and workflows, with content tools, execution, and review integrations.

 This repository provides the Web SDK's core architecture and engine implementations under Apache-2.0 : content models and snapshot formats, plugin and dependency management, the command system, formula and rendering engines, Facade APIs, UI foundation, and Sheets and Docs editing capabilities. Commercial Web SDK plugins, Server SDK, and commercial AI SDK extensions are distributed and licensed separately.

 Agents can use the same open-source APIs; your application supplies the model and tool orchestration. The quotation example demonstrates editing, calculation, and saving without an AI SDK dependency.

 Open-source capabilities

 Area
 Selected capabilities

 Sheets · Editing and layout
 Cell styles, merged cells, in-cell rich text, freeze panes, floating images, and undo/redo.

 Sheets · Data and calculation
 Formulas, defined names, filtering, sorting, data validation, conditional formatting, hyperlinks, comments, and find and replace.

 Docs
 Rich-text editing, paragraph formatting, lists, hyperlinks, comments, and drawing integration.

 Features are composed through plugins and presets; the quick start uses only the Sheets Core preset . Images use the corresponding drawing plugins. See the feature comparison for detailed open-source and commercial coverage.

 The demos below showcase the wider Univer Office SDK , including commercial capabilities. They show more than the default open-source setup; see open source and commercial extensions for scope.

 🚀 Build on the open-source foundation

 Your goal
 Use the open-source foundation
 Start here

 Embed Sheets or Docs
 Add an editable Office surface to your application or agent product, and connect your data through Facade APIs.
 Quick start

 Process content without an editor
 Reuse content plugins, models, commands, and calculation in Node.js for editing, snapshots, and automated tasks.
 Headless guide

 Develop custom features or editors
 Reuse the engines, UI components, plugin boundaries, dependency injection, and command/undo systems. Follow existing features to extend Sheets and Docs or develop your own editors.
 Open-source architecture

 Coordinate edits and undo/redo across features. Inserting a row inside a filter range changes both the base content and the filter range; undo needs to restore both. Each feature supplies its own changes and undo data, and the command composes their execution and history. The architecture walkthrough explains how to extend these editing workflows.

 Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor

 In a browser application using a bundler such as Vite:

 pnpm add @univerjs/presets @univerjs/preset-sheets-core

 Create the container before initializing Univer:

 < div id =" app " style =" height: 100vh " > </ div >

 import { UniverSheetsCorePreset } from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core'
 import UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/locales/en-US'
 import { createUniver , LocaleType , mergeLocales } from '@univerjs/presets'
 import '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/lib/index.css'

 const { univerAPI } = createUniver ( {
 locale : LocaleType . EN_US ,
 locales : {
 [ LocaleType . EN_US ] : mergeLocales ( UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS ) ,
 } ,
 presets : [
 UniverSheetsCorePreset ( {
 container : 'app' ,
 } ) ,
 ] ,
 } )

 univerAPI . createWorkbook ( { } )

 Your page now contains a spreadsheet editor. Use the returned univerAPI to work with its content. This example uses open-source packages and needs no commercial Univer license or Server SDK.

 For component frameworks, retain the univer instance returned by createUniver and call univer.dispose() when the component unmounts. See the lifecycle guide .

 Presets compose plugins and register their Facade APIs. For manual control, see the Plugin Mode example below. The installation guide covers both modes, peer dependencies, and framework integrations.

 Keep coordinated @univerjs/* packages on the same version. Commercial packages must use the matching release line; independently released packages such as icons follow their declared compatibility. See the API Stability Policy .

 Connect your application to editable content

 Facade APIs are the application-facing interface to workbooks, worksheets, and ranges. Continue from the quick start to populate a quotation, update a quantity from application code, and read the recalculated total:

 // Wait for formula controllers before editing a newly created workbook.
 await new Promise < void > ( ( resolve ) => {
 if ( univerAPI . getCurrentLifecycleStage ( ) >= univerAPI . Enum . LifecycleStages . Steady ) {
 resolve ( )
 return
 }
 const listener = univerAPI . addEvent ( univerAPI . Event . LifeCycleChanged , ( { stage } ) => {
 if ( stage === univerAPI . Enum . LifecycleStages . Steady ) {
 listener . dispose ( )
 resolve ( )
 }
 } )
 } )

 const workbook = univerAPI . getActiveWorkbook ( ) !
 const sheet = workbook . getActiveSheet ( )

 sheet . getRange ( 'A1:D4' ) . setValues ( [
 [ 'Item' , 'Quantity' , 'Unit price' , 'Amount' ] ,
 [ 'Seats' , 2 , 25 , '=B2*C2' ] ,
 [ 'Support' , 1 , 100 , '=B3*C3' ] ,
 [ 'Total' , '' , '' , '=SUM(D2:D3)' ] ,
 ] )

 // An application control or agent can make the same edit.
 sheet . getRange ( 'B2' ) . setValue ( 4 )

 univerAPI . getFormula ( ) . onCalculationResultApplied ( ) . then ( ( ) => {
 console . log ( sheet . getRange ( 'D4' ) . getValue ( ) ) // 200
 localStorage . setItem ( 'quotation' , JSON . stringify ( workbook . save ( ) ) )
 } ) . catch ( console . error )

 The editor and your application operate on the same workbook; formula changes are recalculated automatically. workbook.save() returns a JSON snapshot containing the workbook and its registered plugin data. Your application owns persistence; this example uses browser storage. On a later page load, after initialization, restore the snapshot instead of creating a blank workbook :

 const saved = localStorage . getItem ( 'quotation' )
 if ( saved ) {
 univerAPI . createWorkbook ( JSON . parse ( saved ) )
 }

 This workflow uses only open-source packages. Snapshot persistence is separate from XLSX import and export, which uses the separately distributed file-conversion capabilities. Use public Facade APIs for application integration; the source links below explain internal implementation and extension points. See the API Stability Policy before depending on an extension point.

 Advanced: compose plugins manually (Plugin Mode)
 Use Plugin Mode when you need precise control over plugin selection, dependencies, or loading. The preset above handles this composition for you.

 This alternative initialization uses the same app container and the Sheets Core preset's browser plugin stack without a Worker. Use it instead of the preset initialization, then run the same quotation example with the returned univerAPI .

 pnpm add @univerjs/core @univerjs/design @univerjs/docs @univerjs/docs-ui \
 @univerjs/engine-formula @univerjs/engine-render @univerjs/network \
 @univerjs/sheets @univerjs/sheets-ui @univerjs/sheets-formula \

representativeRepos.readmeText:
The open protocol that connects any agent to any app.

 Docs · Examples · Spec · Discord

 AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.

 Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent. The same agent can power a web app, a mobile app, a terminal, or Slack.

 Important
 AG-UI 1.0 is here. The protocol now has a stable, frozen specification backed by a JSON Schema, and the TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs are generated from it. 1.0 is backwards compatible in both directions: 0.x agents work with 1.0 clients and vice versa. What changed → · Migration guide →

 Quick start

 Start a new app. The CLI scaffolds a frontend ( CopilotKit on Next.js, or a terminal client) wired to the agent framework you pick:

 npx create-ag-ui-app@latest

 Then follow the printed next steps. The generated templates call OpenAI, so set your key before npm run dev :

 export OPENAI_API_KEY= " sk-... "

 Or speak the protocol directly: a 30-line agent server and client

 An AG-UI agent is any HTTP endpoint that accepts a RunAgentInput and streams events back. No API keys needed for this one.

 1. The agent (Python). Requires Python 3.9+.

 pip install ag-ui-protocol fastapi uvicorn

 # server.py
 import uuid

 from fastapi import FastAPI , Request
 from fastapi . responses import StreamingResponse
 from ag_ui . core import (
 PROTOCOL_VERSION ,
 RunAgentInput ,
 RunStartedEvent ,
 RunFinishedEvent ,
 TextMessageStartEvent ,
 TextMessageContentEvent ,
 TextMessageEndEvent ,
)
 from ag_ui . encoder import EventEncoder

 app = FastAPI ()

 @ app . post ( "/" )
 async def run_agent ( input_data : RunAgentInput , request : Request ):
 encoder = EventEncoder ( accept = request . headers . get ( "accept" ))

 async def events ():
 yield encoder . encode ( RunStartedEvent (
 thread_id = input_data . thread_id ,
 run_id = input_data . run_id ,
 protocol_version = PROTOCOL_VERSION ,
 ))
 message_id = str ( uuid . uuid4 ())
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageStartEvent ( message_id = message_id , role = "assistant" ))
 for chunk in [ "Hello " , "from " , "AG-UI!" ]:
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageContentEvent ( message_id = message_id , delta = chunk ))
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageEndEvent ( message_id = message_id ))
 yield encoder . encode ( RunFinishedEvent ( thread_id = input_data . thread_id , run_id = input_data . run_id ))

 return StreamingResponse ( events (), media_type = encoder . get_content_type ())

 uvicorn server:app --port 8000

 2. The client (TypeScript). In a second terminal, in a new folder. Requires Node.js 20+.

 npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module
npm install @ag-ui/client tsx

 // client.ts
 import { HttpAgent } from "@ag-ui/client" ;

 const agent = new HttpAgent ( { url : "http://localhost:8000/" } ) ;

 agent . addMessage ( { id : crypto . randomUUID ( ) , role : "user" , content : "Hi there!" } ) ;

 await agent . runAgent ( { } , {
 onRunStartedEvent : ( { event } ) => console . log ( `run started (AG-UI ${ event . protocolVersion } )` ) ,
 onTextMessageContentEvent : ( { event } ) => { process . stdout . write ( event . delta ) ; } ,
 onRunFinishedEvent : ( ) => console . log ( "\nrun finished" ) ,
 } ) ;

 npx tsx client.ts

 You should see Hello from AG-UI! stream in. Swap the server for any supported framework and the client doesn't change.

 Where AG-UI fits

 AG-UI is one of three open, complementary agentic protocols. MCP gives agents tools and context, A2A lets agents work with other agents, and AG-UI brings agents to users. A single agent often uses all three, and AG-UI can front agents that speak MCP or A2A. Read more →

 Note
 AG-UI or A2UI? They work together. A2UI , MCP Apps, and Open-JSON-UI are generative UI specs : they describe what UI an agent wants to show. AG-UI is the runtime protocol that carries those payloads, along with everything else, between the agent and the app. Learn more →

 Integrations

 AG-UI is adopted by Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle, and built into most agent frameworks. Every framework below has a live demo in the Dojo .

 +11 more

 Protocols: A2A · MCP · MCP Apps · A2UI

 Clients: CopilotKit (React, Angular, Vue, React Native) · Slack & Teams · Terminal · OpenBot

 Don't see your framework? Build an integration →

 Full list of integrations

 Show all integrations

- Partners: LangChain · CrewAI

- Built in: Microsoft Agent Framework · Google ADK ( JS ) · Google Antigravity · AWS Strands Agents · Mastra · Pydantic AI · Agno · LlamaIndex · AG2

- More frameworks: Claude Agent SDK · Claude Managed Agents · IBM watsonx Orchestrate · Langroid · Spring AI · Cloudflare Agents · Omnara · Genkit (Go) · OpenAI Agents

- Specs: Oracle Agent Spec

- Deployment: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

 Source for every integration lives in integrations/ and middlewares/ , and the demos in apps/dojo .

 SDKs

 Language
 Install
 Reference

 TypeScript

 Docs · Source

 pip install ag-ui-protocol
 Docs · Source

 dotnet add package AGUI.Client
 Docs · Source

 Community SDKs: Kotlin · Go · Java · Dart · Rust · Ruby · C++ · Swift

 Features: what you can build

 Each building block maps to events in the spec, and each has a live demo in the AG-UI Dojo .

 Building block
 What it does
 Try it

 Streaming chat
 Token-by-token messages across multi-turn sessions, with cancel and resume
 Demo

 Generative UI
 Agents render typed components, or declarative UI with A2UI and MCP Apps
 Demo

 Shared state
 A typed store the agent and app both read and write, synced with snapshots and JSON Patch deltas
 Demo

 Frontend tools
 The agent calls tools that run in the app, and gets the result back
 Demo

 Human in the loop
 Runs end with an interrupt outcome; the user approves, edits, or rejects, and the next run resumes
 Demo

 Reasoning
 Show the agent's reasoning as it works, including encrypted reasoning round-trips
 Demo

 Subagents
 Nested delegation, with every event attributed to the subagent run that produced it
 Demo

 Multimodal
 Images, audio, video, and documents in user input and tool results
 Demo

 Tool output streaming, backend tool rendering, activity progress, token usage, and custom events are covered in the docs . Here's a quick tour of the Dojo:

 dojo.mp4

 How it works

 Your app starts a run by sending the agent a single RunAgentInput : the conversation, the tools the frontend offers, shared state, and context. The agent answers with a stream of typed events from eight families: run lifecycle, text messages, tool calls, state, reasoning, activity, subagents, and custom events ( full list ). Only the run lifecycle is required, so a minimal agent emits a handful of events and grows from there.

 AG-UI is transport-agnostic. The spec defines HTTP + SSE and a binary HTTP + Protobuf binding, and middleware can adapt events from any source. Read the architecture overview for the full picture.

 Event reference

 AG-UI 1.0 defines 31 event types in eight families. See the spec for every field.

 Event family
 Events

 Runs and steps
 RUN_STARTED RUN_FINISHED RUN_ERROR STEP_STARTED STEP_FINISHED

 Text messages
 TEXT_MESSAGE_START TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT TEXT_MESSAGE_END TEXT_MESSAGE_CHUNK

 Tool calls
 TOOL_CALL_START TOOL_CALL_ARGS TOOL_CALL_END TOOL_CALL_RESULT TOOL_CALL_CHUNK

 State
 STATE_SNAPSHOT STATE_DELTA (JSON Patch) MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT

 Reasoning
 REASONING_START REASONING_MESSAGE_* REASONING_ENCRYPTED_VALUE REASONING_END

 Activity
 ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT ACTIVITY_DELTA

 Subagents
 SUBAGENT_STARTED SUBAGENT_FINISHED SUBAGENT_ERROR

 Passthrough
 RAW CUSTOM

 Community

- Questions and ideas: Discord and GitHub Discussions

- Bugs: GitHub Issues

- What's next: the roadmap and the draft spec

 Contributing

 Contributions are welcome: new integrations, SDKs, docs, and fixes. Start with CONTRIBUTING.md , and use the server starter and middleware starter as templates for new integrations. Report security issues as described in SECURITY.md .

 AG-UI was created by CopilotKit and is developed in the open with the community.

 License

 loopforge-promo-v11-en.mp4

 80-second product tour (1080p, with sound).

 LoopForge is a self-hosted workspace where your team ships software with coding agents. Describe what you need to Main Bot in chat: it opens a Docker sandbox, checks out your repositories, delegates to project roles, and opens the PR. When a way of working proves itself, save it as an SOP (a standard workflow of agents, scripts and human gates) so the next requirement is delivered the same way, with review and approval built in.

 Coding-agent CLIs do the work: CodeBuddy, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Antigravity, Kimi Code, Pi, DeepSeek Harness and ZCode. LoopForge adds the roles, sandboxes, checkpoints and history around them, all on your own infrastructure under the MIT license.

 Two ways to work

 Chat with Main Bot
 Run an SOP

 Best for
 Exploring, quick fixes, iterating with the agent
 Repeatable delivery with fixed stages and sign-off

 How it runs
 Main Bot opens a conversation workspace (a Docker sandbox with your repos) on demand and calls project roles as subagents
 The engine runs Agent, Script, Human-gate and sub-SOP nodes in order, in their own sandbox

 You stay in control by
 Queuing or steering messages mid-reply, and pausing, resuming or taking over a running SOP from chat
 Approving at human gates, sending work back to a chosen step, retrying or rerunning from any node

 Delivers
 A PR/MR, or a direct merge into a shared branch ( mode=direct )
 Documents, code or a PR, plus per-node artifacts and logs

 Both paths track the same requirements , so every change, whether made in chat or by an SOP, links back to what was asked for and counts toward delivery and cost reports.

 The chat home. Type a request, @ a role, skill, requirement, SOP or repository, and pick the executor, model and permission mode per conversation.

 Why LoopForge

 Ask a coding agent to "fix this bug" and the result depends on that run. It might skip the plan, forget the tests, review its own code, or stop halfway without anyone noticing. That's fine for a demo, but it isn't how a team ships.

- Repeatable. Same SOP, same stages, same checks for every requirement. Start from built-in backend, frontend, bug-fix and product SOPs.

- Separated roles. Planning, implementation, review and testing each get their own prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills and MCP tools. A role works as an SOP node or as a subagent in chat.

- Human in the loop. Approval gates where they matter. Read the report, approve, or send the work back to a chosen step.

- Observable and resumable. Node status, tool traces, logs and artifacts in one place. Pause, retry a failed step, or rerun from any node.

- Your stack, your servers. Ten coding-agent CLIs as executors, from CodeBuddy, Codex and Claude Code to OpenCode, Cursor CLI and more. GitHub, Skills and MCP as tools. Docker sandboxes or your own machine as the runtime.

 Quick start

 Install Git and clone the repository first. The installer checks Docker, Compose, Python 3 and curl and offers to install missing components. Python/curl installation supports apt, dnf and yum on Linux; the Compose plugin supports x86_64/arm64 and verifies the official release SHA-256. macOS needs a working Python 3 and Docker Desktop; Homebrew can install missing components. Ordinary Linux users are supported through Docker group access or sudo. Set LOOPFORGE_YES=1 to accept installation prompts. Package and image downloads require internet access.

 git clone https://github.com/Tencent/LoopForge.git
 cd LoopForge
./start.sh

 ./start.sh pulls the GHCR release image pinned in compose.yaml without building locally ( bash scripts/install.sh does the same). It creates the MySQL and platform services, generates configuration and session secrets, and installs the built-in sandboxes, starter SOPs and welcome project. Host Go and Node.js installations are not required. Configure model API keys and GitHub authorization after startup. Use ./start.sh logs , stop , restart or pull to manage it, and ./start.sh dev to build the checkout from source.

 If downloads from ghcr.io stall, set MIRROR to a registry host that can stand in for ghcr.io . ./start.sh pulls from that host and tags the image back to the name pinned in compose.yaml . Setting MIRROR trusts that host, because the download is tagged with the official name. The GitHub Release records the digest; docker image inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' ghcr.io/tencent/loopforge:<pin> should show the same digest after @ . Without MIRROR , ./start.sh still pulls ghcr.io directly, and compose.yaml stays unchanged. Upgrade with the same variable and ./start.sh pull . ghcr.nju.edu.cn is one such host. A Docker registry-mirrors entry such as https://docker.nju.edu.cn only accelerates Docker Hub and is not a value for MIRROR .

 MIRROR=ghcr.nju.edu.cn ./start.sh

 Open the address printed by the installer and create your account; the first one becomes the administrator. The service listens on 0.0.0.0:8090 by default. On a cloud host, the installer reads the public IP from the provider's metadata service and prints it; allow the port in your security group, or put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front. Restrict access to your own IP until the administrator account exists. The home page's quick-access guide walks you through adding a model key, connecting a repository and choosing an SOP.

 For GitLab, Gitea, Gogs and other Git hosts, set up Git SSH to check out and push branches with a personal key. PR/MR and Issue automation requires a hosting API token or a separately configured MCP.

 Try it without an API key

 New accounts join the LoopForge demo project , which includes an SOP made only of a script and a human gate:

- Switch to the demo project, open Templates , and open Platform check · script & approval .

- Click Run SOP . A real script writes a report, then the run waits for you at the approval step.

- Approve it from Needs review or the run page, and watch the run continue to its final artifact.

 What you need for real work

 I want to…
 You need

 Run the script + approval demo
 Nothing

 Chat with Main Bot, generate a document or a new project
 An API key for the selected executor

 Change an existing repository (in chat or via an SOP) and open a PR
 Model credentials and a GitHub repository (connect GitHub in personal settings)

 More setup details : executors, GitHub, sandboxes, access model

-
 Executors. Pick one of ten CLIs beside the home composer, then a model. Every SOP role can choose its executor independently (built-in roles default to CodeBuddy). Requirement clarification, AI notification summaries, Bot replies and run evals currently use CodeBuddy, so their model pickers list CodeBuddy models only and the server refuses a model of another CLI instead of switching it to CodeBuddy; scheduled assistant tasks run on the CLI the task selects.

 Executor
 Credentials
 Installation

 CodeBuddy
 Personal key, or a shared key an administrator configures for chat and SOP runs
 In the Docker image

 Codex
 Personal key; a connected execution machine can use its local login
 In the Docker image

 Claude Code
 Personal key; a connected execution machine can use its local login
 Installed from npm on first use, then cached

 OpenCode · Kimi Code · Pi
 Personal key only
 Installed from npm on first use, then cached

 DeepSeek Harness
 Personal key only
 In the Docker image

 Cursor CLI · Antigravity
 Personal key only
 Provider installer on first chat use; not installed into SOP sandboxes

 ZCode
 Personal key only
 Not bundled; install it on the service or execution machine PATH

 The seven agent CLIs after Claude Code keep their model and MCP configuration in a private home directory per run, so they always use the responsible user's own key and Base URL from personal settings, even on a connected execution machine. When rolling them out to a team, each member configures their own credentials. First-use installs need npm or provider access; native deployments need the CLI for the executor you choose.

-
 GitHub is optional. All built-in generic SOPs run without a repository: product SOPs deliver documents, and new frontend/backend projects deliver source files in the task workspace. Bug fixes still need source code and reproduction details. Connect a repository when you work on existing code or want PRs.

-
 Delivering to a repository. Choose Connect GitHub in personal settings, approve the device code on GitHub and pick your repository (the LoopForge OAuth App is built in; no PAT required, manual PAT entry still works). Set executor credentials (or bind a local execution machine), then either run a project SOP or ask Main Bot to change the code and submit a PR/MR.

-
 Sandboxes. In the default Compose installation, SOP runs and conversation workspaces both use Docker sandbox containers started through the host Docker socket. Default sandboxes reuse the installed runtime image, so nothing extra is built after installation; custom Dockerfiles still build their own images. Docker socket access grants control of the host daemon, so this setup is for trusted teams, not untrusted multi-tenant isolation. See deployment boundaries . Re-running the installer keeps your data.

-
 Accounts and access. New installations listen on all interfaces (existing bind settings are kept) and are designed for a trusted team: signed-in users can read project data across the instance, and teammates can sign up from the login page ( AGENTFLOW_ALLOW_SIGNUP=false in .env turns that off). Read the account and access model before exposing it beyond your team.

-
 Remote access, HTTPS, separate workers. See Deployment .

-
 Hacking on LoopForge itself? bash scripts/dev.sh runs it natively (Go 1.26.11+).

 How SOPs work

 An SOP is the workflow a delivery follows. Agents, scripts and people take part in the same run:

 The SOP designer with the built-in bug-fix SOP. Each step picks a role; failed checks can send the work back to an earlier step.

 Node
 What it does

 Agent
 A role (prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills and MCP tools) that designs, implements, reviews or tests.

 Script
 A deterministic shell step: build, test, lint, generate a report. No AI where AI is not needed.

 Human gate
 Pauses the run until someone checks the artifacts and approves, or sends the work back to a step.

 Sub-SOP
 Runs another SOP as a sub-workflow.

 Preview build
 Builds a static site and archives it for review.

 Each node declares its artifacts and dependencies, and the engine starts each step once its dependencies complete. Start from a built-in SOP, adapt its roles, rules and environment to your project, and publish versions as it evolves.

 A run waiting at a human gate: approve and continue, add context and rerun the step, or send the work back upstream.

 A delivery we actually ran: four CodeBuddy roles planned a Python fix, implemented it, reviewed it independently and summarized the delivery. Three real tests passed; the run waited for human approval, then verified the accepted code had not changed. The reusable acceptance case checks the files and results. See the validation record for scope and known gaps.

 Features

 Area
 What you get

 Chat workbench
 Main Bot with per-conversation executor, model and permission mode. @ references for roles, skills, requirements, SOPs and repositories. Messages queue while a reply runs; Steer interrupts and sends now. Generated files open in a side panel with preview, source and download.

 Conversation workspaces
 On-demand Docker sandboxes with the project's repositories checked out, project roles as native subagents, and direct control of a running SOP workspace: pause, resume or take over.

 SOP designer
 Visual canvas with Agent, Script, Human gate, Sub-SOP and Preview nodes, rework-on-failure edges, validation, version history...

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Superpowers

 Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

 Table of Contents

- How it works

- Commercial Services

- Getting Started

- Claude Code

- Antigravity

- Codex App

- Codex CLI

- Cursor

- Devin CLI

- Factory Droid

- Gemini CLI

- GitHub Copilot CLI

- Grok Build CLI

- Kimi Code

- OpenCode

- Pi

- Qwen Code

- Hermes Agent

- Muse

- The Basic Workflow

- When Something Goes Wrong

- Community

- What's Inside

- Philosophy

- Contributing

- Updating

- License

- Visual companion telemetry

 How it works

 It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it doesn't just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do.

 Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest.

 After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY.

 Next up, once you say "go", it launches a subagent-driven-development process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

 There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

 Commercial Services

 If you're using Superpowers in enterprise and could benefit from commercial support, additional tooling, or managed spending, please don't hesitate to drop us a line at sales@primeradiant.com .

 Installation

 Installation differs by harness. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one.

 Claude Code

 Superpowers is available via the official Claude plugin marketplace

 Official Marketplace

-
 Install the plugin from Anthropic's official marketplace:

 /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official

 Superpowers Marketplace

 The Superpowers marketplace provides Superpowers and some other related plugins for Claude Code.

-
 Register the marketplace:

 /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace

-
 Install the plugin from this marketplace:

 /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

 Antigravity

 Install Superpowers as a plugin from this repository:

 agy plugin install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

 Antigravity lists each installed skill's description, and the description of
the using-superpowers skill prompts the model to load that skill at the start
of a conversation. Reinstall with the same command to update.

 Codex App

 Superpowers is available via the official Codex plugin marketplace .

- In the Codex app, click on Plugins in the sidebar.

- You should see Superpowers in the Coding section.

- Click the + next to Superpowers and follow the prompts.

 Codex CLI

 Superpowers is available via the official Codex plugin marketplace .

-
 Open the plugin search interface:

 /plugins

-
 Search for Superpowers:

 superpowers

-
 Select Install Plugin .

 Cursor

-
 In Cursor Agent chat, install from marketplace:

 /add-plugin superpowers

-
 Or search for "superpowers" in the plugin marketplace.

 Devin CLI

-
 Install the plugin from this repository:

 devin plugins install obra/superpowers

-
 Update to the latest version with:

 devin plugins update superpowers

 Factory Droid

-
 Register the marketplace:

 droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Install the plugin:

 droid plugin install superpowers@superpowers

 Gemini CLI

-
 Install the extension:

 gemini extensions install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Update later:

 gemini extensions update superpowers

 GitHub Copilot CLI

-
 Register the marketplace:

 copilot plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace

-
 Install the plugin:

 copilot plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

 Grok Build CLI

 Superpowers is available via the official Grok plugin marketplace .

-
 Install the plugin from xAI's official marketplace:

 grok plugin install superpowers@xai-official --trust

-
 Or open the marketplace in the TUI, search for Superpowers, and install it:

 /marketplace

 Kimi Code

 Superpowers is available in Kimi Code's plugin marketplace.

-
 Open Kimi Code's plugin manager:

 /plugins

-
 Go to Marketplace > Superpowers and install it.

-
 Or install directly from this repository:

 /plugins install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Detailed docs: docs/README.kimi.md

 OpenCode

 OpenCode uses its own plugin install; install Superpowers separately even if you
already use it in another harness.

-
 Tell OpenCode:

 Fetch and follow instructions from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obra/superpowers/refs/heads/main/.opencode/INSTALL.md

-
 Detailed docs: docs/README.opencode.md

 Pi

 Install Superpowers as a Pi package from this repository:

 pi install git:github.com/obra/superpowers

 For local development, run Pi with this checkout loaded as a temporary package:

 pi -e /path/to/superpowers

 The Pi package loads the Superpowers skills and a small extension that injects the using-superpowers bootstrap at session startup and again after compaction. Pi has native skills, so no compatibility Skill tool is required. Subagent and task-list tools remain optional Pi companion packages.

 Qwen Code

 Qwen Code installs plugins from Claude Code marketplaces directly.

-
 Install the plugin from this repository, and pick superpowers when prompted:

 qwen extensions install obra/superpowers

-
 Update later:

 qwen extensions update superpowers

 Hermes Agent

 Install Superpowers as a Hermes plugin from this repository:

 hermes plugins install obra/superpowers --enable

 Restart any active Hermes sessions after installing. Note: Hermes has no
post-compaction hook, so a very long session that compacts over its first
turn loses the bootstrap — start a fresh session if skills stop triggering.

 Muse

 Superpowers is available as a native Muse plugin — same repo, same skills, all harnesses. The using-superpowers bootstrap is injected via the native SessionStart hook alongside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Pi, and the rest — no per-session opt-in.

-
 Install from a local checkout:

 muse plugins install ./
muse plugins approve superpowers

 Or clone and install:

 git clone https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git
muse plugins install ./superpowers
muse plugins approve superpowers

-
 Update later:

 muse plugins update superpowers

 Restart any active Muse sessions after installing so the SessionStart hook takes effect — skills are active immediately, hooks require approval on first install. To verify, start a fresh session and send Let's make a react todo list — a working install auto-triggers brainstorming before any code is written. Version is tracked in .version-bump.json so scripts/bump-version.sh keeps it in sync.

 The Basic Workflow

-
 brainstorming - Activates before building anything. Draws out what you actually want, and why, through questions that get you describing it, then plays its understanding back for correction. Small changes get agreed in chat; projects get a written design document a builder could plan from.

-
 using-git-worktrees - Activates after design approval. Creates isolated workspace on new branch, runs project setup, verifies clean test baseline.

-
 writing-plans - Activates with approved design. Breaks work into bite-sized tasks (2-5 minutes each). Every task has exact file paths, complete code, verification steps.

-
 subagent-driven-development or executing-plans - Activates with plan. Either dispatches a fresh subagent per task with a review after each (most thorough), or implements every task inline in the current session with one fresh review of the whole branch at the end (cheapest).

-
 test-driven-development - Activates during implementation. Enforces RED-GREEN-REFACTOR: write failing test, watch it fail, write minimal code, watch it pass, commit. Deletes code written before tests.

-
 requesting-code-review - Activates between tasks. Reviews against plan, reports issues by severity. Critical issues block progress.

-
 finishing-a-development-branch - Activates when tasks complete. Verifies tests, presents options (merge/PR/keep/discard), cleans up worktree.

 The agent checks for relevant skills before any task. Mandatory workflows, not suggestions.

 When Something Goes Wrong

 Sometimes a session misbehaves: a skill fires when it shouldn't, stays silent when it should, or the agent ignores its plan, repeats work, or burns more tokens than you'd expect. Ask your coding agent to "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in this session" and it will invoke the diagnosing-superpowers skill. To examine an earlier session, name it: "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in session <id> ".

 The skill reads the session transcript, reports what happened with line-level evidence, and, if you want, packages a scrubbed bundle for a bug report.

 Community

 Superpowers is built by Jesse Vincent and the rest of the folks at Prime Radiant .

- Discord : Join us for community support, questions, and sharing what you're building with Superpowers

- Issues : https://github.com/obra/superpowers/issues

- Release announcements : Sign up to get notified about new versions

 What's Inside

 Skills Library

 Testing

- test-driven-development - RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle (includes testing anti-patterns reference)

 Debugging

- systematic-debugging - 4-phase root cause process (includes root-cause-tracing, defense-in-depth, condition-based-waiting techniques)

- verification-before-completion - Ensure it's actually fixed

- diagnosing-superpowers - Work out what went wrong in a session, with evidence; export a scrubbed bundle or file an issue

 Collaboration

- brainstorming - Drawing out intent before building

- writing-plans - Detailed implementation plans

- executing-plans - Inline plan execution: one context, one final review

- dispatching-parallel-agents - Concurrent subagent workflows

- requesting-code-review - Pre-review checklist

- receiving-code-review - Responding to feedback

- using-git-worktrees - Parallel development branches

- finishing-a-development-branch - Merge/PR decision workflow

- subagent-driven-development - Fast iteration with two-stage review (spec compliance, then code quality)

 Meta

- writing-skills - Create new skills following best practices (includes testing methodology)

- using-superpowers - Introduction to the skills system

 Philosophy

- Test-Driven Development - Write tests first, always

- Systematic over ad-hoc - Process over guessing

- Complexity reduction - Simplicity as primary goal

- Evidence over claims - Verify before declaring success

 Read the original release announcement .

 Contributing

 The general contribution process for Superpowers is below. Keep in mind that we don't generally accept contributions of new skills and that any updates to skills must work across all of the coding agents we support. We also don't accept agent-written PRs that fix issues filed by someone else unless a maintainer asked for one, even when you hit the same problem; add your report to the existing issue instead.

- Fork the repository

- Switch to the 'dev' branch

- Create a branch for your work

- Follow the writing-skills skill for creating and testing new and modified skills

- Submit a PR, filling in every section of the pull request template, including the sum...

Build your own AI office with Univer Office SDK.

 Start with open-source Sheets and Docs, then connect your own application or agent.

 🚀 Quick start · 💼 Workspace · 📚 Documentation · ⚖️ Feature comparison · 🌐 Website · 🎮 Showcase · 🔧 API Reference · 📝 Blog

 English · Français · Deutsch · Español · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어

 Table of contents

- 💡 What is Univer?

- Open-source capabilities

- 🚀 Build on the open-source foundation

- Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor

- Connect your application to editable content

- 🏗️ Explore the open-source architecture

- Give custom features clear boundaries

- Compose cross-feature edits and undo/redo

- Connect applications and agents through Facade APIs and events

- 🧩 Extend your application with Univer Office SDK

- Scope and licensing

- 🌐 Application patterns and ecosystem

- Univer Workspace: an Office SDK reference application

- CLI, agent integrations, and developer skills

- 📚 Documentation and contributing

- 💬 Community

- ❤️ Sponsors

 💡 What is Univer?

 Univer is an Office SDK for building Office applications inside your own product. It provides Office editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing for people and existing agents, using your data and permissions. The product family covers spreadsheets, documents, presentations, relational tables, canvases, and PDFs.

 Univer Office SDK has three parts:

- Web SDK is the foundation: content models, editing, rendering, formula calculation, and Facade APIs (application-facing APIs). Compose its plugins into an embedded editor or your own Office application, and reuse the content models, commands, and calculation for Headless processing without an interactive editor.

- Server SDK adds backend services for real-time collaboration, edit history, and Office file import and export.

- AI SDK connects Office capabilities to existing agents and workflows, with content tools, execution, and review integrations.

 This repository provides the Web SDK's core architecture and engine implementations under Apache-2.0 : content models and snapshot formats, plugin and dependency management, the command system, formula and rendering engines, Facade APIs, UI foundation, and Sheets and Docs editing capabilities. Commercial Web SDK plugins, Server SDK, and commercial AI SDK extensions are distributed and licensed separately.

 Agents can use the same open-source APIs; your application supplies the model and tool orchestration. The quotation example demonstrates editing, calculation, and saving without an AI SDK dependency.

 Open-source capabilities

 Area
 Selected capabilities

 Sheets · Editing and layout
 Cell styles, merged cells, in-cell rich text, freeze panes, floating images, and undo/redo.

 Sheets · Data and calculation
 Formulas, defined names, filtering, sorting, data validation, conditional formatting, hyperlinks, comments, and find and replace.

 Docs
 Rich-text editing, paragraph formatting, lists, hyperlinks, comments, and drawing integration.

 Features are composed through plugins and presets; the quick start uses only the Sheets Core preset . Images use the corresponding drawing plugins. See the feature comparison for detailed open-source and commercial coverage.

 The demos below showcase the wider Univer Office SDK , including commercial capabilities. They show more than the default open-source setup; see open source and commercial extensions for scope.

 🚀 Build on the open-source foundation

 Your goal
 Use the open-source foundation
 Start here

 Embed Sheets or Docs
 Add an editable Office surface to your application or agent product, and connect your data through Facade APIs.
 Quick start

 Process content without an editor
 Reuse content plugins, models, commands, and calculation in Node.js for editing, snapshots, and automated tasks.
 Headless guide

 Develop custom features or editors
 Reuse the engines, UI components, plugin boundaries, dependency injection, and command/undo systems. Follow existing features to extend Sheets and Docs or develop your own editors.
 Open-source architecture

 Coordinate edits and undo/redo across features. Inserting a row inside a filter range changes both the base content and the filter range; undo needs to restore both. Each feature supplies its own changes and undo data, and the command composes their execution and history. The architecture walkthrough explains how to extend these editing workflows.

 Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor

 In a browser application using a bundler such as Vite:

 pnpm add @univerjs/presets @univerjs/preset-sheets-core

 Create the container before initializing Univer:

 < div id =" app " style =" height: 100vh " > </ div >

 import { UniverSheetsCorePreset } from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core'
 import UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/locales/en-US'
 import { createUniver , LocaleType , mergeLocales } from '@univerjs/presets'
 import '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/lib/index.css'

 const { univerAPI } = createUniver ( {
 locale : LocaleType . EN_US ,

 Connect your application to editable content

 Facade APIs are the application-facing interface to workbooks, worksheets, and ranges. Continue from the quick start to populate a quotation, update a quantity from application code, and read the recalculated total:

 return
 }

 if ( stage === univerAPI . Enum . LifecycleStages . Steady ) {
 listener . dispose ( )
 resolve ( )
 }
 } )
 } )

 [ 'Item' , 'Quantity' , 'Unit price' , 'Amount' ] ,
 [ 'Seats' , 2 , 25 , '=B2*C2' ] ,
 [ 'Support' , 1 , 100 , '=B3*C3' ] ,
 [ 'Total' , '' , '' , '=SUM(D2:D3)' ] ,
 ] )

 sheet . getRange ( 'B2' ) . setValue ( 4 )

 } ) . catch ( console . error )

Your application owns persistence; this example uses browser storage. On a later page load, after initialization, restore the snapshot instead of creating a blank workbook :

 const saved = localStorage . getItem ( 'quotation' )
 if ( saved ) {
 univerAPI . createWorkbook ( JSON . parse ( saved ) )
 }

 This workflow uses only open-source packages. Snapshot persistence is separate from XLSX import and export, which uses the separately distributed file-conversion capabilities. Use public Facade APIs for application integration; the source links below explain internal implementation and extension points. See the API Stability Policy before depending on an extension point.

 Advanced: compose plugins manually (Plugin Mode)
 Use Plugin Mode when you need precise control over plugin selection, dependencies, or loading. The preset above handles this composition for you.

representativeRepos.readmeText:
The open protocol that connects any agent to any app.

 Docs · Examples · Spec · Discord

 AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.

 Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent. The same agent can power a web app, a mobile app, a terminal, or Slack.

 Important
 AG-UI 1.0 is here. The protocol now has a stable, frozen specification backed by a JSON Schema, and the TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs are generated from it. 1.0 is backwards compatible in both directions: 0.x agents work with 1.0 clients and vice versa. What changed → · Migration guide →

 Quick start

 Start a new app. The CLI scaffolds a frontend ( CopilotKit on Next.js, or a terminal client) wired to the agent framework you pick:

 npx create-ag-ui-app@latest

 Then follow the printed next steps. The generated templates call OpenAI, so set your key before npm run dev :

 export OPENAI_API_KEY= " sk-... "

 Or speak the protocol directly: a 30-line agent server and client

 An AG-UI agent is any HTTP endpoint that accepts a RunAgentInput and streams events back. No API keys needed for this one.

 1. The agent (Python). Requires Python 3.9+.

 pip install ag-ui-protocol fastapi uvicorn

 # server.py
 import uuid

 from fastapi import FastAPI , Request
 from fastapi . responses import StreamingResponse
 from ag_ui . core import (
 PROTOCOL_VERSION ,
 RunAgentInput ,
 RunStartedEvent ,
 RunFinishedEvent ,
 TextMessageStartEvent ,
 TextMessageContentEvent ,
 TextMessageEndEvent ,
)
 from ag_ui . encoder import EventEncoder

 app = FastAPI ()

 @ app . post ( "/" )
 async def run_agent ( input_data : RunAgentInput , request : Request ):
 encoder = EventEncoder ( accept = request . headers . get ( "accept" ))

 async def events ():
 yield encoder . encode ( RunStartedEvent (
 thread_id = input_data . thread_id ,
 run_id = input_data . run_id ,
 protocol_version = PROTOCOL_VERSION ,
 ))
 message_id = str ( uuid . uuid4 ())
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageStartEvent ( message_id = message_id , role = "assistant" ))
 for chunk in [ "Hello " , "from " , "AG-UI!" ]:
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageContentEvent ( message_id = message_id , delta = chunk ))
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageEndEvent ( message_id = message_id ))
 yield encoder . encode ( RunFinishedEvent ( thread_id = input_data . thread_id , run_id = input_data . run_id ))

 return StreamingResponse ( events (), media_type = encoder . get_content_type ())

 uvicorn server:app --port 8000

 2. The client (TypeScript). In a second terminal, in a new folder. Requires Node.js 20+.

 npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module
npm install @ag-ui/client tsx

 // client.ts
 import { HttpAgent } from "@ag-ui/client" ;

 const agent = new HttpAgent ( { url : "http://localhost:8000/" } ) ;

 agent . addMessage ( { id : crypto . randomUUID ( ) , role : "user" , content : "Hi there!" } ) ;

 await agent . runAgent ( { } , {
 onRunStartedEvent : ( { event } ) => console . log ( `run started (AG-UI ${ event . protocolVersion } )` ) ,
 onTextMessageContentEvent : ( { event } ) => { process . stdout . write ( event . delta ) ; } ,
 onRunFinishedEvent : ( ) => console . log ( "\nrun finished" ) ,
 } ) ;

 npx tsx client.ts

 You should see Hello from AG-UI! stream in. Swap the server for any supported framework and the client doesn't change.

 Where AG-UI fits

 AG-UI is one of three open, complementary agentic protocols. MCP gives agents tools and context, A2A lets agents work with other agents, and AG-UI brings agents to users. A single agent often uses all three, and AG-UI can front agents that speak MCP or A2A. Read more →

 Note
 AG-UI or A2UI? They work together. A2UI , MCP Apps, and Open-JSON-UI are generative UI specs : they describe what UI an agent wants to show. AG-UI is the runtime protocol that carries those payloads, along with everything else, between the agent and the app. Learn more →

 Integrations

 AG-UI is adopted by Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle, and built into most agent frameworks. Every framework below has a live demo in the Dojo .

- Built in: Microsoft Agent Framework · Google ADK ( JS ) · Google Antigravity · AWS Strands Agents · Mastra · Pydantic AI · Agno · LlamaIndex · AG2

- More frameworks: Claude Agent SDK · Claude Managed Agents · IBM watsonx Orchestrate · Langroid · Spring AI · Cloudflare Agents · Omnara · Genkit (Go) · OpenAI Agents

 Features: what you can build

 Each building block maps to events in the spec, and each has a live demo in the AG-UI Dojo .

 Building block
 What it does
 Try it

 Streaming chat
 Token-by-token messages across multi-turn sessions, with cancel and resume
 Demo

 Generative UI

 Demo

 Shared state
 A typed store the agent and app both read and write, synced with snapshots and JSON Patch deltas
 Demo

 Frontend tools
 The agent calls tools that run in the app, and gets the result back
 Demo

 Human in the loop
 Runs end with an interrupt outcome; the user approves, edits, or rejects, and the next run resumes
 Demo

 Reasoning
 Show the agent's reasoning as it works, including encrypted reasoning round-trips
 Demo

 Subagents
 Nested delegation, with every event attributed to the subagent run that produced it
 Demo

 Multimodal
 Images, audio, video, and documents in user input and tool results
 Demo

 Tool output streaming, backend tool rendering, activity progress, token usage, and custom events are covered in the docs . Here's a quick tour of the Dojo:

 dojo.mp4

 How it works

 Your app starts a run by sending the agent a single RunAgentInput : the conversation, the tools the frontend offers, shared state, and context. The agent answers with a stream of typed events from eight families: run lifecycle, text messages, tool calls, state, reasoning, activity, subagents, and custom events ( full list ). Only the run lifecycle is required, so a minimal agent emits a handful of events and grows from there.

 AG-UI is transport-agnostic. The spec defines HTTP + SSE and a binary HTTP + Protobuf binding, and middleware can adapt events from any source. Read the architecture overview for the full picture.

 Event reference

 AG-UI 1.0 defines 31 event types in eight families. See the spec for every field.

 Event family
 Events

 Runs and steps
 RUN_STARTED RUN_FINISHED RUN_ERROR STEP_STARTED STEP_FINISHED

 Text messages
 TEXT_MESSAGE_START TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT TEXT_MESSAGE_END TEXT_MESSAGE_CHUNK

 Tool calls
 TOOL_CALL_START TOOL_CALL_ARGS TOOL_CALL_END TOOL_CALL_RESULT TOOL_CALL_CHUNK

 State
 STATE_SNAPSHOT STATE_DELTA (JSON Patch) MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT

 Reasoning
 REASONING_START REASONING_MESSAGE_* REASONING_ENCRYPTED_VALUE REASONING_END

 Activity
 ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT ACTIVITY_DELTA

 Subagents
 SUBAGENT_STARTED SUBAGENT_FINISHED SUBAGENT_ERROR

 Passthrough
 RAW CUSTOM

 Community

- Questions and ideas: Discord and GitHub Discussions

- Bugs: GitHub Issues

- What's next: the roadmap and the draft spec

 Contributing

 Contributions are welcome: new integrations, SDKs, docs, and fixes. Start with CONTRIBUTING.md , and use the server starter and middleware starter as templates for new integrations. Report security issues as described in SECURITY.md .

 AG-UI was created by CopilotKit and is developed in the open with the community.
