 💡 What is Univer?

 Univer is an Office SDK for building Office applications inside your own product. It provides Office editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing for people and existing agents, using your data and permissions. The product family covers spreadsheets, documents, presentations, relational tables, canvases, and PDFs.

 Univer Office SDK has three parts:

- Web SDK is the foundation: content models, editing, rendering, formula calculation, and Facade APIs (application-facing APIs). Compose its plugins into an embedded editor or your own Office application, and reuse the content models, commands, and calculation for Headless processing without an interactive editor.

- Server SDK adds backend services for real-time collaboration, edit history, and Office file import and export.

- AI SDK connects Office capabilities to existing agents and workflows, with content tools, execution, and review integrations.

 This repository provides the Web SDK's core architecture and engine implementations under Apache-2.0 : content models and snapshot formats, plugin and dependency management, the command system, formula and rendering engines, Facade APIs, UI foundation, and Sheets and Docs editing capabilities. Commercial Web SDK plugins, Server SDK, and commercial AI SDK extensions are distributed and licensed separately.

 Agents can use the same open-source APIs; your application supplies the model and tool orchestration. The quotation example demonstrates editing, calculation, and saving without an AI SDK dependency.

 Open-source capabilities

 Area
 Selected capabilities

 Sheets · Editing and layout
 Cell styles, merged cells, in-cell rich text, freeze panes, floating images, and undo/redo.

 Sheets · Data and calculation
 Formulas, defined names, filtering, sorting, data validation, conditional formatting, hyperlinks, comments, and find and replace.

 Docs
 Rich-text editing, paragraph formatting, lists, hyperlinks, comments, and drawing integration.

 Features are composed through plugins and presets; the quick start uses only the Sheets Core preset . Images use the corresponding drawing plugins. See the feature comparison for detailed open-source and commercial coverage.

 The demos below showcase the wider Univer Office SDK , including commercial capabilities. They show more than the default open-source setup; see open source and commercial extensions for scope.

 🚀 Build on the open-source foundation

 Your goal
 Use the open-source foundation
 Start here

 Embed Sheets or Docs
 Add an editable Office surface to your application or agent product, and connect your data through Facade APIs.
 Quick start

 Process content without an editor
 Reuse content plugins, models, commands, and calculation in Node.js for editing, snapshots, and automated tasks.
 Headless guide

 Develop custom features or editors
 Reuse the engines, UI components, plugin boundaries, dependency injection, and command/undo systems. Follow existing features to extend Sheets and Docs or develop your own editors.
 Open-source architecture

 Coordinate edits and undo/redo across features. Inserting a row inside a filter range changes both the base content and the filter range; undo needs to restore both. Each feature supplies its own changes and undo data, and the command composes their execution and history. The architecture walkthrough explains how to extend these editing workflows.

 Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor

 In a browser application using a bundler such as Vite:

 pnpm add @univerjs/presets @univerjs/preset-sheets-core

 Create the container before initializing Univer:

 < div id =" app " style =" height: 100vh " > </ div >

 import { UniverSheetsCorePreset } from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core'
 import UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/locales/en-US'
 import { createUniver , LocaleType , mergeLocales } from '@univerjs/presets'
 import '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/lib/index.css'

 const { univerAPI } = createUniver ( {
 locale : LocaleType . EN_US ,
 locales : {
 [ LocaleType . EN_US ] : mergeLocales ( UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS ) ,
 } ,
 presets : [
 UniverSheetsCorePreset ( {
 container : 'app' ,
 } ) ,
 ] ,
 } )

 univerAPI . createWorkbook ( { } )

 Your page now contains a spreadsheet editor. Use the returned univerAPI to work with its content. This example uses open-source packages and needs no commercial Univer license or Server SDK.

 For component frameworks, retain the univer instance returned by createUniver and call univer.dispose() when the component unmounts. See the lifecycle guide .

 Presets compose plugins and register their Facade APIs. For manual control, see the Plugin Mode example below. The installation guide covers both modes, peer dependencies, and framework integrations.

 Keep coordinated @univerjs/* packages on the same version. Commercial packages must use the matching release line; independently released packages such as icons follow their declared compatibility. See the API Stability Policy .

 Connect your application to editable content

 Facade APIs are the application-facing interface to workbooks, worksheets, and ranges. Continue from the quick start to populate a quotation, update a quantity from application code, and read the recalculated total:

 // Wait for formula controllers before editing a newly created workbook.
 await new Promise < void > ( ( resolve ) => {
 if ( univerAPI . getCurrentLifecycleStage ( ) >= univerAPI . Enum . LifecycleStages . Steady ) {
 resolve ( )
 return
 }
 const listener = univerAPI . addEvent ( univerAPI . Event . LifeCycleChanged , ( { stage } ) => {
 if ( stage === univerAPI . Enum . LifecycleStages . Steady ) {
 listener . dispose ( )
 resolve ( )
 }
 } )
 } )

 const workbook = univerAPI . getActiveWorkbook ( ) !
 const sheet = workbook . getActiveSheet ( )

 sheet . getRange ( 'A1:D4' ) . setValues ( [
 [ 'Item' , 'Quantity' , 'Unit price' , 'Amount' ] ,
 [ 'Seats' , 2 , 25 , '=B2*C2' ] ,
 [ 'Support' , 1 , 100 , '=B3*C3' ] ,
 [ 'Total' , '' , '' , '=SUM(D2:D3)' ] ,
 ] )

 // An application control or agent can make the same edit.
 sheet . getRange ( 'B2' ) . setValue ( 4 )

 univerAPI . getFormula ( ) . onCalculationResultApplied ( ) . then ( ( ) => {
 console . log ( sheet . getRange ( 'D4' ) . getValue ( ) ) // 200
 localStorage . setItem ( 'quotation' , JSON . stringify ( workbook . save ( ) ) )
 } ) . catch ( console . error )

 The editor and your application operate on the same workbook; formula changes are recalculated automatically. workbook.save() returns a JSON snapshot containing the workbook and its registered plugin data. Your application owns persistence; this example uses browser storage. On a later page load, after initialization, restore the snapshot instead of creating a blank workbook :

 const saved = localStorage . getItem ( 'quotation' )
 if ( saved ) {
 univerAPI . createWorkbook ( JSON . parse ( saved ) )
 }

 This workflow uses only open-source packages. Snapshot persistence is separate from XLSX import and export, which uses the separately distributed file-conversion capabilities. Use public Facade APIs for application integration; the source links below explain internal implementation and extension points. See the API Stability Policy before depending on an extension point.

 Advanced: compose plugins manually (Plugin Mode)
 Use Plugin Mode when you need precise control over plugin selection, dependencies, or loading. The preset above handles this composition for you.

 This alternative initialization uses the same app container and the Sheets Core preset's browser plugin stack without a Worker. Use it instead of the preset initialization, then run the same quotation example with the returned univerAPI .

representativeRepos.readmeText:
The open protocol that connects any agent to any app.

 Docs · Examples · Spec · Discord

 AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.

 Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent. The same agent can power a web app, a mobile app, a terminal, or Slack.

 Important
 AG-UI 1.0 is here. The protocol now has a stable, frozen specification backed by a JSON Schema, and the TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs are generated from it. 1.0 is backwards compatible in both directions: 0.x agents work with 1.0 clients and vice versa. What changed → · Migration guide →

 Quick start

 Start a new app. The CLI scaffolds a frontend ( CopilotKit on Next.js, or a terminal client) wired to the agent framework you pick:

 npx create-ag-ui-app@latest

 Then follow the printed next steps. The generated templates call OpenAI, so set your key before npm run dev :

 export OPENAI_API_KEY= " sk-... "

 Or speak the protocol directly: a 30-line agent server and client

 An AG-UI agent is any HTTP endpoint that accepts a RunAgentInput and streams events back. No API keys needed for this one.

 1. The agent (Python). Requires Python 3.9+.

 pip install ag-ui-protocol fastapi uvicorn

 # server.py
 import uuid

 from fastapi import FastAPI , Request
 from fastapi . responses import StreamingResponse
 from ag_ui . core import (
 PROTOCOL_VERSION ,
 RunAgentInput ,
 RunStartedEvent ,
 RunFinishedEvent ,
 TextMessageStartEvent ,
 TextMessageContentEvent ,
 TextMessageEndEvent ,
)
 from ag_ui . encoder import EventEncoder

 app = FastAPI ()

 @ app . post ( "/" )
 async def run_agent ( input_data : RunAgentInput , request : Request ):
 encoder = EventEncoder ( accept = request . headers . get ( "accept" ))

 async def events ():
 yield encoder . encode ( RunStartedEvent (
 thread_id = input_data . thread_id ,
 run_id = input_data . run_id ,
 protocol_version = PROTOCOL_VERSION ,
 ))
 message_id = str ( uuid . uuid4 ())
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageStartEvent ( message_id = message_id , role = "assistant" ))
 for chunk in [ "Hello " , "from " , "AG-UI!" ]:
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageContentEvent ( message_id = message_id , delta = chunk ))
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageEndEvent ( message_id = message_id ))
 yield encoder . encode ( RunFinishedEvent ( thread_id = input_data . thread_id , run_id = input_data . run_id ))

 return StreamingResponse ( events (), media_type = encoder . get_content_type ())

 uvicorn server:app --port 8000

 2. The client (TypeScript). In a second terminal, in a new folder. Requires Node.js 20+.

 npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module
npm install @ag-ui/client tsx

 // client.ts
 import { HttpAgent } from "@ag-ui/client" ;

 const agent = new HttpAgent ( { url : "http://localhost:8000/" } ) ;

 agent . addMessage ( { id : crypto . randomUUID ( ) , role : "user" , content : "Hi there!" } ) ;

 await agent . runAgent ( { } , {
 onRunStartedEvent : ( { event } ) => console . log ( `run started (AG-UI ${ event . protocolVersion } )` ) ,
 onTextMessageContentEvent : ( { event } ) => { process . stdout . write ( event . delta ) ; } ,
 onRunFinishedEvent : ( ) => console . log ( "\nrun finished" ) ,
 } ) ;

 npx tsx client.ts

 You should see Hello from AG-UI! stream in. Swap the server for any supported framework and the client doesn't change.

 Where AG-UI fits

 AG-UI is one of three open, complementary agentic protocols. MCP gives agents tools and context, A2A lets agents work with other agents, and AG-UI brings agents to users. A single agent often uses all three, and AG-UI can front agents that speak MCP or A2A. Read more →

 Note
 AG-UI or A2UI? They work together. A2UI , MCP Apps, and Open-JSON-UI are generative UI specs : they describe what UI an agent wants to show. AG-UI is the runtime protocol that carries those payloads, along with everything else, between the agent and the app. Learn more →

 Integrations

 AG-UI is adopted by Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle, and built into most agent frameworks. Every framework below has a live demo in the Dojo .

 Community SDKs: Kotlin · Go · Java · Dart · Rust · Ruby · C++ · Swift

 Features: what you can build

 Each building block maps to events in the spec, and each has a live demo in the AG-UI Dojo .

 Building block
 What it does
 Try it

 Streaming chat
 Token-by-token messages across multi-turn sessions, with cancel and resume
 Demo

 Generative UI
 Agents render typed components, or declarative UI with A2UI and MCP Apps
 Demo

 Shared state
 A typed store the agent and app both read and write, synced with snapshots and JSON Patch deltas
 Demo

 Frontend tools
 The agent calls tools that run in the app, and gets the result back
 Demo

 Human in the loop
 Runs end with an interrupt outcome; the user approves, edits, or rejects, and the next run resumes
 Demo

 Reasoning
 Show the agent's reasoning as it works, including encrypted reasoning round-trips
 Demo

 Subagents
 Nested delegation, with every event attributed to the subagent run that produced it
 Demo

 Multimodal
 Images, audio, video, and documents in user input and tool results
 Demo

 Tool output streaming, backend tool rendering, activity progress, token usage, and custom events are covered in the docs . Here's a quick tour of the Dojo:

 dojo.mp4

 How it works

 Your app starts a run by sending the agent a single RunAgentInput : the conversation, the tools the frontend offers, shared state, and context. The agent answers with a stream of typed events from eight families: run lifecycle, text messages, tool calls, state, reasoning, activity, subagents, and custom events ( full list ). Only the run lifecycle is required, so a minimal agent emits a handful of events and grows from there.

 AG-UI is transport-agnostic. The spec defines HTTP + SSE and a binary HTTP + Protobuf binding, and middleware can adapt events from any source. Read the architecture overview for the full picture.

 Event reference

 AG-UI 1.0 defines 31 event types in eight families. See the spec for every field.

 Event family
 Events

 Runs and steps
 RUN_STARTED RUN_FINISHED RUN_ERROR STEP_STARTED STEP_FINISHED

 Text messages
 TEXT_MESSAGE_START TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT TEXT_MESSAGE_END TEXT_MESSAGE_CHUNK

 Tool calls
 TOOL_CALL_START TOOL_CALL_ARGS TOOL_CALL_END TOOL_CALL_RESULT TOOL_CALL_CHUNK

 State
 STATE_SNAPSHOT STATE_DELTA (JSON Patch) MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT

 Reasoning
 REASONING_START REASONING_MESSAGE_* REASONING_ENCRYPTED_VALUE REASONING_END

 Activity
 ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT ACTIVITY_DELTA

 Subagents
 SUBAGENT_STARTED SUBAGENT_FINISHED SUBAGENT_ERROR

 Passthrough
 RAW CUSTOM

 Community

- Questions and ideas: Discord and GitHub Discussions

- Bugs: GitHub Issues

- What's next: the roadmap and the draft spec

 Contributing

 Contributions are welcome: new integrations, SDKs, docs, and fixes. Start with CONTRIBUTING.md , and use the server starter and middleware starter as templates for new integrations. Report security issues as described in SECURITY.md .

 AG-UI was created by CopilotKit and is developed in the open with the community.

Superpowers

 Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

 Table of Contents

- License

- Visual companion telemetry

 How it works

 It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it doesn't just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do.

 Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest.

 After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY.

 Next up, once you say "go", it launches a subagent-driven-development process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

 There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

 Commercial Services

 If you're using Superpowers in enterprise and could benefit from commercial support, additional tooling, or managed spending, please don't hesitate to drop us a line at sales@primeradiant.com .

 Installation

 Installation differs by harness. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one.

 Claude Code

 Superpowers is available via the official Claude plugin marketplace

 Official Marketplace

-
 Install the plugin from Anthropic's official marketplace:

 /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official

 Superpowers Marketplace

 The Superpowers marketplace provides Superpowers and some other related plugins for Claude Code.

-
 Register the marketplace:

 /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace

-
 Install the plugin from this marketplace:

 /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

 Antigravity

 Install Superpowers as a plugin from this repository:

 agy plugin install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

 Antigravity lists each installed skill's description, and the description of
the using-superpowers skill prompts the model to load that skill at the start
of a conversation. Reinstall with the same command to update.

 Codex App

 Superpowers is available via the official Codex plugin marketplace .

- In the Codex app, click on Plugins in the sidebar.

- You should see Superpowers in the Coding section.

- Click the + next to Superpowers and follow the prompts.

 Codex CLI

 Superpowers is available via the official Codex plugin marketplace .

-
 Open the plugin search interface:

 /plugins

-
 Search for Superpowers:

 superpowers

-
 Select Install Plugin .

 Cursor

-
 In Cursor Agent chat, install from marketplace:

 /add-plugin superpowers

-
 Or search for "superpowers" in the plugin marketplace.

 Devin CLI

-
 Install the plugin from this repository:

 devin plugins install obra/superpowers

-
 Update to the latest version with:

 devin plugins update superpowers

 Factory Droid

-
 Register the marketplace:

 droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Install the plugin:

 droid plugin install superpowers@superpowers

 Gemini CLI

-
 Install the extension:

 gemini extensions install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Update later:

 gemini extensions update superpowers

 GitHub Copilot CLI

-
 Register the marketplace:

 copilot plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace

-
 Install the plugin:

 copilot plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

 Grok Build CLI

 Superpowers is available via the official Grok plugin marketplace .

-
 Install the plugin from xAI's official marketplace:

 grok plugin install superpowers@xai-official --trust

-
 Or open the marketplace in the TUI, search for Superpowers, and install it:

 /marketplace

 Kimi Code

 Superpowers is available in Kimi Code's plugin marketplace.

-
 Open Kimi Code's plugin manager:

 /plugins

-
 Go to Marketplace > Superpowers and install it.

-
 Or install directly from this repository:

 /plugins install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Detailed docs: docs/README.kimi.md

 OpenCode

 OpenCode uses its own plugin install; install Superpowers separately even if you
already use it in another harness.

-
 Tell OpenCode:

 Fetch and follow instructions from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obra/superpowers/refs/heads/main/.opencode/INSTALL.md

-
 Detailed docs: docs/README.opencode.md

 Pi

 Install Superpowers as a Pi package from this repository:

 pi install git:github.com/obra/superpowers

 For local development, run Pi with this checkout loaded as a temporary package:

 pi -e /path/to/superpowers

 The Pi package loads the Superpowers skills and a small extension that injects the using-superpowers bootstrap at session startup and again after compaction. Pi has native skills, so no compatibility Skill tool is required. Subagent and task-list tools remain optional Pi companion packages.

 Qwen Code

 Qwen Code installs plugins from Claude Code marketplaces directly.

-
 Install the plugin from this repository, and pick superpowers when prompted:

 qwen extensions install obra/superpowers

-
 Update later:

 qwen extensions update superpowers

 Hermes Agent

 Install Superpowers as a Hermes plugin from this repository:

 hermes plugins install obra/superpowers --enable

 Restart any active Hermes sessions after installing. Note: Hermes has no
post-compaction hook, so a very long session that compacts over its first
turn loses the bootstrap — start a fresh session if skills stop triggering.

 Muse

 Superpowers is available as a native Muse plugin — same repo, same skills, all harnesses. The using-superpowers bootstrap is injected via the native SessionStart hook alongside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Pi, and the rest — no per-session opt-in.

-
 Install from a local checkout:

 muse plugins install ./
muse plugins approve superpowers

 Or clone and install:

 git clone https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git
muse plugins install ./superpowers
muse plugins approve superpowers

-
 Update later:

 muse plugins update superpowers

 Restart any active Muse sessions after installing so the SessionStart hook takes effect — skills are active immediately, hooks require approval on first install. To verify, start a fresh session and send Let's make a react todo list — a working install auto-triggers brainstorming before any code is written. Version is tracked in .version-bump.json so scripts/bump-version.sh keeps it in sync.

 The Basic Workflow

-
 brainstorming - Activates before building anything. Draws out what you actually want, and why, through questions that get you describing it, then plays its understanding back for correction. Small changes get agreed in chat; projects get a written design document a builder could plan from.

-
 using-git-worktrees - Activates after design approval. Creates isolated workspace on new branch, runs project setup, verifies clean test baseline.

-
 writing-plans - Activates with approved design. Breaks work into bite-sized tasks (2-5 minutes each). Every task has exact file paths, complete code, verification steps.

-
 subagent-driven-development or executing-plans - Activates with plan. Either dispatches a fresh subagent per task with a review after each (most thorough), or implements every task inline in the current session with one fresh review of the whole branch at the end (cheapest).

-
 test-driven-development - Activates during implementation. Enforces RED-GREEN-REFACTOR: write failing test, watch it fail, write minimal code, watch it pass, commit. Deletes code written before tests.

-
 requesting-code-review - Activates between tasks. Reviews against plan, reports issues by severity. Critical issues block progress.

-
 finishing-a-development-branch - Activates when tasks complete. Verifies tests, presents options (merge/PR/keep/discard), cleans up worktree.

 The agent checks for relevant skills before any task. Mandatory workflows, not suggestions.

 When Something Goes Wrong

 Sometimes a session misbehaves: a skill fires when it shouldn't, stays silent when it should, or the agent ignores its plan, repeats work, or burns more tokens than you'd expect. Ask your coding agent to "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in this session" and it will invoke the diagnosing-superpowers skill. To examine an earlier session, name it: "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in session <id> ".

 The skill reads the session transcript, reports what happened with line-level evidence, and, if you want, packages a scrubbed bundle for a bug report.

 Community

 Superpowers is built by Jesse Vincent and the rest of the folks at Prime Radiant .

- Discord : Join us for community support, questions, and sharing what you're building with Superpowers

- Issues : https://github.com/obra/superpowers/issues

- Release announcements : Sign up to get notified about new versions

 Philosophy

- Test-Driven Development - Write tests first, always

- Systematic over ad-hoc - Process over guessing

- Complexity reduction - Simplicity as primary goal

- Evidence over claims - Verify before declaring success

 💡 What is Univer?

 Univer is an Office SDK for building Office applications inside your own product. It provides Office editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing for people and existing agents, using your data and permissions. The product family covers spreadsheets, documents, presentations, relational tables, canvases, and PDFs.

 Univer Office SDK has three parts:

- Web SDK is the foundation: content models, editing, rendering, formula calculation, and Facade APIs (application-facing APIs). Compose its plugins into an embedded editor or your own Office application, and reuse the content models, commands, and calculation for Headless processing without an interactive editor.

- Server SDK adds backend services for real-time collaboration, edit history, and Office file import and export.

- AI SDK connects Office capabilities to existing agents and workflows, with content tools, execution, and review integrations.

 This repository provides the Web SDK's core architecture and engine implementations under Apache-2.0 : content models and snapshot formats, plugin and dependency management, the command system, formula and rendering engines, Facade APIs, UI foundation, and Sheets and Docs editing capabilities. Commercial Web SDK plugins, Server SDK, and commercial AI SDK extensions are distributed and licensed separately.

 Agents can use the same open-source APIs; your application supplies the model and tool orchestration. The quotation example demonstrates editing, calculation, and saving without an AI SDK dependency.

 Open-source capabilities

 Area
 Selected capabilities

 Sheets · Editing and layout
 Cell styles, merged cells, in-cell rich text, freeze panes, floating images, and undo/redo.

 Sheets · Data and calculation
 Formulas, defined names, filtering, sorting, data validation, conditional formatting, hyperlinks, comments, and find and replace.

 Docs
 Rich-text editing, paragraph formatting, lists, hyperlinks, comments, and drawing integration.

 Features are composed through plugins and presets; the quick start uses only the Sheets Core preset . Images use the corresponding drawing plugins. See the feature comparison for detailed open-source and commercial coverage.

 The demos below showcase the wider Univer Office SDK , including commercial capabilities. They show more than the default open-source setup; see open source and commercial extensions for scope.

 🚀 Build on the open-source foundation

 Your goal
 Use the open-source foundation
 Start here

 Embed Sheets or Docs
 Add an editable Office surface to your application or agent product, and connect your data through Facade APIs.
 Quick start

 Process content without an editor
 Reuse content plugins, models, commands, and calculation in Node.js for editing, snapshots, and automated tasks.
 Headless guide

 Develop custom features or editors
 Reuse the engines, UI components, plugin boundaries, dependency injection, and command/undo systems. Follow existing features to extend Sheets and Docs or develop your own editors.
 Open-source architecture

 Coordinate edits and undo/redo across features. Inserting a row inside a filter range changes both the base content and the filter range; undo needs to restore both. Each feature supplies its own changes and undo data, and the command composes their execution and history. The architecture walkthrough explains how to extend these editing workflows.

 Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor

 In a browser application using a bundler such as Vite:

 pnpm add @univerjs/presets @univerjs/preset-sheets-core

 Create the container before initializing Univer:

 < div id =" app " style =" height: 100vh " > </ div >

 import { UniverSheetsCorePreset } from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core'
 import UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/locales/en-US'
 import { createUniver , LocaleType , mergeLocales } from '@univerjs/presets'
 import '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/lib/index.css'

 const { univerAPI } = createUniver ( {
 locale : LocaleType . EN_US ,
 locales : {
 [ LocaleType . EN_US ] : mergeLocales ( UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS ) ,
 } ,
 presets : [
 UniverSheetsCorePreset ( {
 container : 'app' ,
 } ) ,
 ] ,
 } )

 univerAPI . createWorkbook ( { } )

 Your page now contains a spreadsheet editor. Use the returned univerAPI to work with its content. This example uses open-source packages and needs no commercial Univer license or Server SDK.

 For component frameworks, retain the univer instance returned by createUniver and call univer.dispose() when the component unmounts. See the lifecycle guide .

 Presets compose plugins and register their Facade APIs. For manual control, see the Plugin Mode example below. The installation guide covers both modes, peer dependencies, and framework integrations.

 Keep coordinated @univerjs/* packages on the same version. Commercial packages must use the matching release line; independently released packages such as icons follow their declared compatibility. See the API Stability Policy .

 Connect your application to editable content

 Facade APIs are the application-facing interface to workbooks, worksheets, and ranges. Continue from the quick start to populate a quotation, update a quantity from application code, and read the recalculated total:

 // Wait for formula controllers before editing a newly created workbook.
 await new Promise < void > ( ( resolve ) => {
 if ( univerAPI . getCurrentLifecycleStage ( ) >= univerAPI . Enum . LifecycleStages . Steady ) {
 resolve ( )
 return
 }
 const listener = univerAPI . addEvent ( univerAPI . Event . LifeCycleChanged , ( { stage } ) => {
 if ( stage === univerAPI . Enum . LifecycleStages . Steady ) {
 listener . dispose ( )
 resolve ( )
 }
 } )
 } )

 const workbook = univerAPI . getActiveWorkbook ( ) !
 const sheet = workbook . getActiveSheet ( )

 sheet . getRange ( 'A1:D4' ) . setValues ( [
 [ 'Item' , 'Quantity' , 'Unit price' , 'Amount' ] ,
 [ 'Seats' , 2 , 25 , '=B2*C2' ] ,
 [ 'Support' , 1 , 100 , '=B3*C3' ] ,
 [ 'Total' , '' , '' , '=SUM(D2:D3)' ] ,
 ] )

 // An application control or agent can make the same edit.
 sheet . getRange ( 'B2' ) . setValue ( 4 )

 univerAPI . getFormula ( ) . onCalculationResultApplied ( ) . then ( ( ) => {
 console . log ( sheet . getRange ( 'D4' ) . getValue ( ) ) // 200
 localStorage . setItem ( 'quotation' , JSON . stringify ( workbook . save ( ) ) )
 } ) . catch ( console . error )

 The editor and your application operate on the same workbook; formula changes are recalculated automatically. workbook.save() returns a JSON snapshot containing the workbook and its registered plugin data. Your application owns persistence; this example uses browser storage. On a later page load, after initialization, restore the snapshot instead of creating a blank workbook :

 const saved = localStorage . getItem ( 'quotation' )
 if ( saved ) {
 univerAPI . createWorkbook ( JSON . parse ( saved ) )
 }

 This workflow uses only open-source packages. Snapshot persistence is separate from XLSX import and export, which uses the separately distributed file-conversion capabilities. Use public Facade APIs for application integration; the source links below explain internal implementation and extension points. See the API Stability Policy before depending on an extension point.

 Advanced: compose plugins manually (Plugin Mode)
 Use Plugin Mode when you need precise control over plugin selection, dependencies, or loading. The preset above handles this composition for you.

 This alternative initialization uses the same app container and the Sheets Core preset's browser plugin stack without a Worker. Use it instead of the preset initialization, then run the same quotation example with the returned univerAPI .

representativeRepos.readmeText:
The open protocol that connects any agent to any app.

 Docs · Examples · Spec · Discord

 AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.

 Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent. The same agent can power a web app, a mobile app, a terminal, or Slack.

 Important
 AG-UI 1.0 is here. The protocol now has a stable, frozen specification backed by a JSON Schema, and the TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs are generated from it. 1.0 is backwards compatible in both directions: 0.x agents work with 1.0 clients and vice versa. What changed → · Migration guide →

 Quick start

 Start a new app. The CLI scaffolds a frontend ( CopilotKit on Next.js, or a terminal client) wired to the agent framework you pick:

 npx create-ag-ui-app@latest

 Then follow the printed next steps. The generated templates call OpenAI, so set your key before npm run dev :

 export OPENAI_API_KEY= " sk-... "

 Or speak the protocol directly: a 30-line agent server and client

 An AG-UI agent is any HTTP endpoint that accepts a RunAgentInput and streams events back. No API keys needed for this one.

 1. The agent (Python). Requires Python 3.9+.

 pip install ag-ui-protocol fastapi uvicorn

 # server.py
 import uuid

 from fastapi import FastAPI , Request
 from fastapi . responses import StreamingResponse
 from ag_ui . core import (
 PROTOCOL_VERSION ,
 RunAgentInput ,
 RunStartedEvent ,
 RunFinishedEvent ,
 TextMessageStartEvent ,
 TextMessageContentEvent ,
 TextMessageEndEvent ,
)
 from ag_ui . encoder import EventEncoder

 app = FastAPI ()

 @ app . post ( "/" )
 async def run_agent ( input_data : RunAgentInput , request : Request ):
 encoder = EventEncoder ( accept = request . headers . get ( "accept" ))

 async def events ():
 yield encoder . encode ( RunStartedEvent (
 thread_id = input_data . thread_id ,
 run_id = input_data . run_id ,
 protocol_version = PROTOCOL_VERSION ,
 ))
 message_id = str ( uuid . uuid4 ())
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageStartEvent ( message_id = message_id , role = "assistant" ))
 for chunk in [ "Hello " , "from " , "AG-UI!" ]:
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageContentEvent ( message_id = message_id , delta = chunk ))
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageEndEvent ( message_id = message_id ))
 yield encoder . encode ( RunFinishedEvent ( thread_id = input_data . thread_id , run_id = input_data . run_id ))

 return StreamingResponse ( events (), media_type = encoder . get_content_type ())

 uvicorn server:app --port 8000

 2. The client (TypeScript). In a second terminal, in a new folder. Requires Node.js 20+.

 npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module
npm install @ag-ui/client tsx

 // client.ts
 import { HttpAgent } from "@ag-ui/client" ;

 const agent = new HttpAgent ( { url : "http://localhost:8000/" } ) ;

 agent . addMessage ( { id : crypto . randomUUID ( ) , role : "user" , content : "Hi there!" } ) ;

 await agent . runAgent ( { } , {
 onRunStartedEvent : ( { event } ) => console . log ( `run started (AG-UI ${ event . protocolVersion } )` ) ,
 onTextMessageContentEvent : ( { event } ) => { process . stdout . write ( event . delta ) ; } ,
 onRunFinishedEvent : ( ) => console . log ( "\nrun finished" ) ,
 } ) ;

 npx tsx client.ts

 You should see Hello from AG-UI! stream in. Swap the server for any supported framework and the client doesn't change.

 Where AG-UI fits

 AG-UI is one of three open, complementary agentic protocols. MCP gives agents tools and context, A2A lets agents work with other agents, and AG-UI brings agents to users. A single agent often uses all three, and AG-UI can front agents that speak MCP or A2A. Read more →

 Note
 AG-UI or A2UI? They work together. A2UI , MCP Apps, and Open-JSON-UI are generative UI specs : they describe what UI an agent wants to show. AG-UI is the runtime protocol that carries those payloads, along with everything else, between the agent and the app. Learn more →

 Integrations

 AG-UI is adopted by Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle, and built into most agent frameworks. Every framework below has a live demo in the Dojo .

 Protocols: A2A · MCP · MCP Apps · A2UI

 Clients: CopilotKit (React, Angular, Vue, React Native) · Slack & Teams · Terminal · OpenBot

 Don't see your framework? Build an integration →

 Full list of integrations

 Show all integrations

- Partners: LangChain · CrewAI

- Built in: Microsoft Agent Framework · Google ADK ( JS ) · Google Antigravity · AWS Strands Agents · Mastra · Pydantic AI · Agno · LlamaIndex · AG2

- More frameworks: Claude Agent SDK · Claude Managed Agents · IBM watsonx Orchestrate · Langroid · Spring AI · Cloudflare Agents · Omnara · Genkit (Go) · OpenAI Agents

- Specs: Oracle Agent Spec

- Deployment: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

 Source for every integration lives in integrations/ and middlewares/ , and the demos in apps/dojo .

 SDKs

 Language
 Install
 Reference

 TypeScript

 Docs · Source

 Docs · Source

 Community SDKs: Kotlin · Go · Java · Dart · Rust · Ruby · C++ · Swift

 Features: what you can build

 Each building block maps to events in the spec, and each has a live demo in the AG-UI Dojo .

 Building block
 What it does
 Try it

 Streaming chat
 Token-by-token messages across multi-turn sessions, with cancel and resume
 Demo

 Generative UI
 Agents render typed components, or declarative UI with A2UI and MCP Apps
 Demo

 Shared state
 A typed store the agent and app both read and write, synced with snapshots and JSON Patch deltas
 Demo

 Frontend tools
 The agent calls tools that run in the app, and gets the result back
 Demo

 Human in the loop
 Runs end with an interrupt outcome; the user approves, edits, or rejects, and the next run resumes
 Demo

 Reasoning
 Show the agent's reasoning as it works, including encrypted reasoning round-trips
 Demo

 Subagents
 Nested delegation, with every event attributed to the subagent run that produced it
 Demo

 Multimodal
 Images, audio, video, and documents in user input and tool results
 Demo

 Tool output streaming, backend tool rendering, activity progress, token usage, and custom events are covered in the docs . Here's a quick tour of the Dojo:

 dojo.mp4

 How it works

 Your app starts a run by sending the agent a single RunAgentInput : the conversation, the tools the frontend offers, shared state, and context. The agent answers with a stream of typed events from eight families: run lifecycle, text messages, tool calls, state, reasoning, activity, subagents, and custom events ( full list ). Only the run lifecycle is required, so a minimal agent emits a handful of events and grows from there.

 AG-UI is transport-agnostic. The spec defines HTTP + SSE and a binary HTTP + Protobuf binding, and middleware can adapt events from any source. Read the architecture overview for the full picture.

 Event reference

 AG-UI 1.0 defines 31 event types in eight families. See the spec for every field.

 Event family
 Events

 Runs and steps
 RUN_STARTED RUN_FINISHED RUN_ERROR STEP_STARTED STEP_FINISHED

 Text messages
 TEXT_MESSAGE_START TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT TEXT_MESSAGE_END TEXT_MESSAGE_CHUNK

 Tool calls
 TOOL_CALL_START TOOL_CALL_ARGS TOOL_CALL_END TOOL_CALL_RESULT TOOL_CALL_CHUNK

 State
 STATE_SNAPSHOT STATE_DELTA (JSON Patch) MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT

 Reasoning
 REASONING_START REASONING_MESSAGE_* REASONING_ENCRYPTED_VALUE REASONING_END

 Activity
 ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT ACTIVITY_DELTA

 Subagents
 SUBAGENT_STARTED SUBAGENT_FINISHED SUBAGENT_ERROR

 Passthrough
 RAW CUSTOM

 Community

- Questions and ideas: Discord and GitHub Discussions

- Bugs: GitHub Issues

- What's next: the roadmap and the draft spec

 Contributing

 Contributions are welcome: new integrations, SDKs, docs, and fixes. Start with CONTRIBUTING.md , and use the server starter and middleware starter as templates for new integrations. Report security issues as described in SECURITY.md .

 AG-UI was created by CopilotKit and is developed in the open with the community.

 License

 AG-UI is open source under the MIT License .

readmeText:
Superpowers

 Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

 Table of Contents

- How it works

- Commercial Services

- Getting Started

- Claude Code

- Antigravity

- Codex App

- Codex CLI

- Cursor

- Devin CLI

- Factory Droid

- Gemini CLI

- GitHub Copilot CLI

- Grok Build CLI

- Kimi Code

- OpenCode

- Pi

- Qwen Code

- Hermes Agent

- Muse

- The Basic Workflow

- When Something Goes Wrong

- Community

- What's Inside

- Philosophy

- Contributing

- Updating

- License

- Visual companion telemetry

 How it works

 It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it doesn't just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do.

 Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest.

 After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY.

 Next up, once you say "go", it launches a subagent-driven-development process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

 There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

 Commercial Services

 If you're using Superpowers in enterprise and could benefit from commercial support, additional tooling, or managed spending, please don't hesitate to drop us a line at sales@primeradiant.com .

 Installation

 Installation differs by harness. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one.

 Claude Code

 Superpowers is available via the official Claude plugin marketplace

 Official Marketplace

-
 Install the plugin from Anthropic's official marketplace:

 /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official

 Superpowers Marketplace

 The Superpowers marketplace provides Superpowers and some other related plugins for Claude Code.

-
 Register the marketplace:

 /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace

-
 Install the plugin from this marketplace:

 /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

 Antigravity

 Install Superpowers as a plugin from this repository:

 agy plugin install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

 Antigravity lists each installed skill's description, and the description of
the using-superpowers skill prompts the model to load that skill at the start
of a conversation. Reinstall with the same command to update.

 Codex App

 Superpowers is available via the official Codex plugin marketplace .

- In the Codex app, click on Plugins in the sidebar.

- You should see Superpowers in the Coding section.

- Click the + next to Superpowers and follow the prompts.

 Codex CLI

 Superpowers is available via the official Codex plugin marketplace .

-
 Open the plugin search interface:

 /plugins

-
 Search for Superpowers:

 superpowers

-
 Select Install Plugin .

 Cursor

-
 In Cursor Agent chat, install from marketplace:

 /add-plugin superpowers

-
 Or search for "superpowers" in the plugin marketplace.

 Devin CLI

-
 Install the plugin from this repository:

 devin plugins install obra/superpowers

-
 Update to the latest version with:

 devin plugins update superpowers

 Factory Droid

-
 Register the marketplace:

 droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Install the plugin:

 droid plugin install superpowers@superpowers

 Gemini CLI

-
 Install the extension:

 gemini extensions install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Update later:

 gemini extensions update superpowers

 GitHub Copilot CLI

-
 Register the marketplace:

 copilot plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace

-
 Install the plugin:

 copilot plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

 Grok Build CLI

 Superpowers is available via the official Grok plugin marketplace .

-
 Install the plugin from xAI's official marketplace:

 grok plugin install superpowers@xai-official --trust

-
 Or open the marketplace in the TUI, search for Superpowers, and install it:

 /marketplace

 Kimi Code

 Superpowers is available in Kimi Code's plugin marketplace.

-
 Open Kimi Code's plugin manager:

 /plugins

-
 Go to Marketplace > Superpowers and install it.

-
 Or install directly from this repository:

 /plugins install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Detailed docs: docs/README.kimi.md

 OpenCode

 OpenCode uses its own plugin install; install Superpowers separately even if you
already use it in another harness.

-
 Tell OpenCode:

 Fetch and follow instructions from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obra/superpowers/refs/heads/main/.opencode/INSTALL.md

-
 Detailed docs: docs/README.opencode.md

 Pi

 Install Superpowers as a Pi package from this repository:

 pi install git:github.com/obra/superpowers

 For local development, run Pi with this checkout loaded as a temporary package:

 pi -e /path/to/superpowers

 The Pi package loads the Superpowers skills and a small extension that injects the using-superpowers bootstrap at session startup and again after compaction. Pi has native skills, so no compatibility Skill tool is required. Subagent and task-list tools remain optional Pi companion packages.

 Qwen Code

 Qwen Code installs plugins from Claude Code marketplaces directly.

-
 Install the plugin from this repository, and pick superpowers when prompted:

 qwen extensions install obra/superpowers

-
 Update later:

 qwen extensions update superpowers

 Hermes Agent

 Install Superpowers as a Hermes plugin from this repository:

 hermes plugins install obra/superpowers --enable

 Restart any active Hermes sessions after installing. Note: Hermes has no
post-compaction hook, so a very long session that compacts over its first
turn loses the bootstrap — start a fresh session if skills stop triggering.

 Muse

 Superpowers is available as a native Muse plugin — same repo, same skills, all harnesses. The using-superpowers bootstrap is injected via the native SessionStart hook alongside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Pi, and the rest — no per-session opt-in.

-
 Install from a local checkout:

 muse plugins install ./
muse plugins approve superpowers

 Or clone and install:

 git clone https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git
muse plugins install ./superpowers
muse plugins approve superpowers

-
 Update later:

 muse plugins update superpowers

 Restart any active Muse sessions after installing so the SessionStart hook takes effect — skills are active immediately, hooks require approval on first install. To verify, start a fresh session and send Let's make a react todo list — a working install auto-triggers brainstorming before any code is written. Version is tracked in .version-bump.json so scripts/bump-version.sh keeps it in sync.

 The Basic Workflow

-
 brainstorming - Activates before building anything. Draws out what you actually want, and why, through questions that get you describing it, then plays its understanding back for correction. Small changes get agreed in chat; projects get a written design document a builder could plan from.

-
 using-git-worktrees - Activates after design approval. Creates isolated workspace on new branch, runs project setup, verifies clean test baseline.

-
 writing-plans - Activates with approved design. Breaks work into bite-sized tasks (2-5 minutes each). Every task has exact file paths, complete code, verification steps.

-
 subagent-driven-development or executing-plans - Activates with plan. Either dispatches a fresh subagent per task with a review after each (most thorough), or implements every task inline in the current session with one fresh review of the whole branch at the end (cheapest).

-
 test-driven-development - Activates during implementation. Enforces RED-GREEN-REFACTOR: write failing test, watch it fail, write minimal code, watch it pass, commit. Deletes code written before tests.

-
 requesting-code-review - Activates between tasks. Reviews against plan, reports issues by severity. Critical issues block progress.

-
 finishing-a-development-branch - Activates when tasks complete. Verifies tests, presents options (merge/PR/keep/discard), cleans up worktree.

 The agent checks for relevant skills before any task. Mandatory workflows, not suggestions.

 When Something Goes Wrong

 Sometimes a session misbehaves: a skill fires when it shouldn't, stays silent when it should, or the agent ignores its plan, repeats work, or burns more tokens than you'd expect. Ask your coding agent to "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in this session" and it will invoke the diagnosing-superpowers skill. To examine an earlier session, name it: "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in session <id> ".

 The skill reads the session transcript, reports what happened with line-level evidence, and, if you want, packages a scrubbed bundle for a bug report.

 Community

 Superpowers is built by Jesse Vincent and the rest of the folks at Prime Radiant .

- Discord : Join us for community support, questions, and sharing what you're building with Superpowers

- Issues : https://github.com/obra/superpowers/issues

- Release announcements : Sign up to get notified about new versions

 What's Inside

 Skills Library

 Testing

- test-driven-development - RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle (includes testing anti-patterns reference)

 Debugging

- systematic-debugging - 4-phase root cause process (includes root-cause-tracing, defense-in-depth, condition-based-waiting techniques)

- verification-before-completion - Ensure it's actually fixed

- diagnosing-superpowers - Work out what went wrong in a session, with evidence; export a scrubbed bundle or file an issue

 Collaboration

- brainstorming - Drawing out intent before building

- writing-plans - Detailed implementation plans

- executing-plans - Inline plan execution: one context, one final review

- dispatching-parallel-agents - Concurrent subagent workflows

- requesting-code-review - Pre-review checklist

- receiving-code-review - Responding to feedback

- using-git-worktrees - Parallel development branches

- finishing-a-development-branch - Merge/PR decision workflow

- subagent-driven-development - Fast iteration with two-stage review (spec compliance, then code quality)

 Meta

- writing-skills - Create new skills following best practices (includes testing methodology)

- using-superpowers - Introduction to the skills system

 Philosophy

- Test-Driven Development - Write tests first, always

- Systematic over ad-hoc - Process over guessing

- Complexity reduction - Simplicity as primary goal

- Evidence over claims - Verify before declaring success

 Read the original release announcement .

 Contributing

 The general contribution process for Superpowers is below. Keep in mind that we don't generally accept contributions of new skills and that any updates to skills must work across all of the coding agents we support. We also don't accept agent-written PRs that fix issues filed by someone else unless a maintainer asked for one, even when you hit the same problem; add your report to the existing issue instead.

- Fork the repository

- Switch to the 'dev' branch

- Create a branch for your work

- Follow the writing-skills skill for creating and testing new and modified skills

- Submit a PR, filling in every section of the pull request template, including the sum...

representativeRepos.readmeText:
Superpowers

 Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

 Table of Contents

- How it works

- Commercial Services

- Getting Started

- Claude Code

- Antigravity

- Codex App

- Codex CLI

- Cursor

- Devin CLI

- Factory Droid

- Gemini CLI

- GitHub Copilot CLI

- Grok Build CLI

- Kimi Code

- OpenCode

- Pi

- Qwen Code

- Hermes Agent

- Muse

- The Basic Workflow

- When Something Goes Wrong

- Community

- What's Inside

- Philosophy

- Contributing

- Updating

- License

- Visual companion telemetry

 How it works

 It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it doesn't just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do.

 Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest.

 After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY.

 Next up, once you say "go", it launches a subagent-driven-development process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

 There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

 Commercial Services

 If you're using Superpowers in enterprise and could benefit from commercial support, additional tooling, or managed spending, please don't hesitate to drop us a line at sales@primeradiant.com .

 Installation

 Installation differs by harness. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one.

 Claude Code

 Superpowers is available via the official Claude plugin marketplace

 Official Marketplace

-
 Install the plugin from Anthropic's official marketplace:

 /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official

 Superpowers Marketplace

 The Superpowers marketplace provides Superpowers and some other related plugins for Claude Code.

-
 Register the marketplace:

 /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace

-
 Install the plugin from this marketplace:

 /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

 Antigravity

 Install Superpowers as a plugin from this repository:

 agy plugin install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

 Antigravity lists each installed skill's description, and the description of
the using-superpowers skill prompts the model to load that skill at the start
of a conversation. Reinstall with the same command to update.

 Codex App

 Superpowers is available via the official Codex plugin marketplace .

- In the Codex app, click on Plugins in the sidebar.

- You should see Superpowers in the Coding section.

- Click the + next to Superpowers and follow the prompts.

 Codex CLI

 Superpowers is available via the official Codex plugin marketplace .

-
 Open the plugin search interface:

 /plugins

-
 Search for Superpowers:

 superpowers

-
 Select Install Plugin .

 Cursor

-
 In Cursor Agent chat, install from marketplace:

 /add-plugin superpowers

-
 Or search for "superpowers" in the plugin marketplace.

 Devin CLI

-
 Install the plugin from this repository:

 devin plugins install obra/superpowers

-
 Update to the latest version with:

 devin plugins update superpowers

 Factory Droid

-
 Register the marketplace:

 droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Install the plugin:

 droid plugin install superpowers@superpowers

 Gemini CLI

-
 Install the extension:

 gemini extensions install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Update later:

 gemini extensions update superpowers

 GitHub Copilot CLI

-
 Register the marketplace:

 copilot plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace

-
 Install the plugin:

 copilot plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

 Grok Build CLI

 Superpowers is available via the official Grok plugin marketplace .

-
 Install the plugin from xAI's official marketplace:

 grok plugin install superpowers@xai-official --trust

-
 Or open the marketplace in the TUI, search for Superpowers, and install it:

 /marketplace

 Kimi Code

 Superpowers is available in Kimi Code's plugin marketplace.

-
 Open Kimi Code's plugin manager:

 /plugins

-
 Go to Marketplace > Superpowers and install it.

-
 Or install directly from this repository:

 /plugins install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

-
 Detailed docs: docs/README.kimi.md

 OpenCode

 OpenCode uses its own plugin install; install Superpowers separately even if you
already use it in another harness.

-
 Tell OpenCode:

 Fetch and follow instructions from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obra/superpowers/refs/heads/main/.opencode/INSTALL.md

-
 Detailed docs: docs/README.opencode.md

 Pi

 Install Superpowers as a Pi package from this repository:

 pi install git:github.com/obra/superpowers

 For local development, run Pi with this checkout loaded as a temporary package:

 pi -e /path/to/superpowers

 The Pi package loads the Superpowers skills and a small extension that injects the using-superpowers bootstrap at session startup and again after compaction. Pi has native skills, so no compatibility Skill tool is required. Subagent and task-list tools remain optional Pi companion packages.

 Qwen Code

 Qwen Code installs plugins from Claude Code marketplaces directly.

-
 Install the plugin from this repository, and pick superpowers when prompted:

 qwen extensions install obra/superpowers

-
 Update later:

 qwen extensions update superpowers

 Hermes Agent

 Install Superpowers as a Hermes plugin from this repository:

 hermes plugins install obra/superpowers --enable

 Restart any active Hermes sessions after installing. Note: Hermes has no
post-compaction hook, so a very long session that compacts over its first
turn loses the bootstrap — start a fresh session if skills stop triggering.

 Muse

 Superpowers is available as a native Muse plugin — same repo, same skills, all harnesses. The using-superpowers bootstrap is injected via the native SessionStart hook alongside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Pi, and the rest — no per-session opt-in.

-
 Install from a local checkout:

 muse plugins install ./
muse plugins approve superpowers

 Or clone and install:

 git clone https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git
muse plugins install ./superpowers
muse plugins approve superpowers

-
 Update later:

 muse plugins update superpowers

 Restart any active Muse sessions after installing so the SessionStart hook takes effect — skills are active immediately, hooks require approval on first install. To verify, start a fresh session and send Let's make a react todo list — a working install auto-triggers brainstorming before any code is written. Version is tracked in .version-bump.json so scripts/bump-version.sh keeps it in sync.

 The Basic Workflow

-
 brainstorming - Activates before building anything. Draws out what you actually want, and why, through questions that get you describing it, then plays its understanding back for correction. Small changes get agreed in chat; projects get a written design document a builder could plan from.

-
 using-git-worktrees - Activates after design approval. Creates isolated workspace on new branch, runs project setup, verifies clean test baseline.

-
 writing-plans - Activates with approved design. Breaks work into bite-sized tasks (2-5 minutes each). Every task has exact file paths, complete code, verification steps.

-
 subagent-driven-development or executing-plans - Activates with plan. Either dispatches a fresh subagent per task with a review after each (most thorough), or implements every task inline in the current session with one fresh review of the whole branch at the end (cheapest).

-
 test-driven-development - Activates during implementation. Enforces RED-GREEN-REFACTOR: write failing test, watch it fail, write minimal code, watch it pass, commit. Deletes code written before tests.

-
 requesting-code-review - Activates between tasks. Reviews against plan, reports issues by severity. Critical issues block progress.

-
 finishing-a-development-branch - Activates when tasks complete. Verifies tests, presents options (merge/PR/keep/discard), cleans up worktree.

 The agent checks for relevant skills before any task. Mandatory workflows, not suggestions.

 When Something Goes Wrong

 Sometimes a session misbehaves: a skill fires when it shouldn't, stays silent when it should, or the agent ignores its plan, repeats work, or burns more tokens than you'd expect. Ask your coding agent to "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in this session" and it will invoke the diagnosing-superpowers skill. To examine an earlier session, name it: "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in session <id> ".

 The skill reads the session transcript, reports what happened with line-level evidence, and, if you want, packages a scrubbed bundle for a bug report.

 Community

 Superpowers is built by Jesse Vincent and the rest of the folks at Prime Radiant .

- Discord : Join us for community support, questions, and sharing what you're building with Superpowers

- Issues : https://github.com/obra/superpowers/issues

- Release announcements : Sign up to get notified about new versions

 What's Inside

 Skills Library

 Testing

- test-driven-development - RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle (includes testing anti-patterns reference)

 Debugging

- systematic-debugging - 4-phase root cause process (includes root-cause-tracing, defense-in-depth, condition-based-waiting techniques)

- verification-before-completion - Ensure it's actually fixed

- diagnosing-superpowers - Work out what went wrong in a session, with evidence; export a scrubbed bundle or file an issue

 Collaboration

- brainstorming - Drawing out intent before building

- writing-plans - Detailed implementation plans

- executing-plans - Inline plan execution: one context, one final review

- dispatching-parallel-agents - Concurrent subagent workflows

- requesting-code-review - Pre-review checklist

- receiving-code-review - Responding to feedback

- using-git-worktrees - Parallel development branches

- finishing-a-development-branch - Merge/PR decision workflow

- subagent-driven-development - Fast iteration with two-stage review (spec compliance, then code quality)

 Meta

- writing-skills - Create new skills following best practices (includes testing methodology)

- using-superpowers - Introduction to the skills system

 Philosophy

- Test-Driven Development - Write tests first, always

- Systematic over ad-hoc - Process over guessing

- Complexity reduction - Simplicity as primary goal

- Evidence over claims - Verify before declaring success

 Read the original release announcement .

 Contributing

 The general contribution process for Superpowers is below. Keep in mind that we don't generally accept contributions of new skills and that any updates to skills must work across all of the coding agents we support. We also don't accept agent-written PRs that fix issues filed by someone else unless a maintainer asked for one, even when you hit the same problem; add your report to the existing issue instead.

- Fork the repository

- Switch to the 'dev' branch

- Create a branch for your work

- Follow the writing-skills skill for creating and testing new and modified skills

- Submit a PR, filling in every section of the pull request template, including the sum...

Build your own AI office with Univer Office SDK.

 Start with open-source Sheets and Docs, then connect your own application or agent.

 🚀 Quick start · 💼 Workspace · 📚 Documentation · ⚖️ Feature comparison · 🌐 Website · 🎮 Showcase · 🔧 API Reference · 📝 Blog

 English · Français · Deutsch · Español · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어

 Table of contents

- 💡 What is Univer?

- Open-source capabilities

- 🚀 Build on the open-source foundation

- Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor

- Connect your application to editable content

- 🏗️ Explore the open-source architecture

- Give custom features clear boundaries

- Compose cross-feature edits and undo/redo

- Connect applications and agents through Facade APIs and events

- 🧩 Extend your application with Univer Office SDK

- Scope and licensing

- 🌐 Application patterns and ecosystem

- Univer Workspace: an Office SDK reference application

- CLI, agent integrations, and developer skills

- 📚 Documentation and contributing

- Runtime compatibility

- 💬 Community

- 🔒 Security

- ❤️ Sponsors

- 📄 License

 💡 What is Univer?

 Univer is an Office SDK for building Office applications inside your own product. It provides Office editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing for people and existing agents, using your data and permissions. The product family covers spreadsheets, documents, presentations, relational tables, canvases, and PDFs.

 Univer Office SDK has three parts:

- Web SDK is the foundation: content models, editing, rendering, formula calculation, and Facade APIs (application-facing APIs). Compose its plugins into an embedded editor or your own Office application, and reuse the content models, commands, and calculation for Headless processing without an interactive editor.

- Server SDK adds backend services for real-time collaboration, edit history, and Office file import and export.

- AI SDK connects Office capabilities to existing agents and workflows, with content tools, execution, and review integrations.

 This repository provides the Web SDK's core architecture and engine implementations under Apache-2.0 : content models and snapshot formats, plugin and dependency management, the command system, formula and rendering engines, Facade APIs, UI foundation, and Sheets and Docs editing capabilities. Commercial Web SDK plugins, Server SDK, and commercial AI SDK extensions are distributed and licensed separately.

 Agents can use the same open-source APIs; your application supplies the model and tool orchestration. The quotation example demonstrates editing, calculation, and saving without an AI SDK dependency.

 Open-source capabilities

 Area
 Selected capabilities

 Sheets · Editing and layout
 Cell styles, merged cells, in-cell rich text, freeze panes, floating images, and undo/redo.

 Sheets · Data and calculation
 Formulas, defined names, filtering, sorting, data validation, conditional formatting, hyperlinks, comments, and find and replace.

 Docs
 Rich-text editing, paragraph formatting, lists, hyperlinks, comments, and drawing integration.

 Features are composed through plugins and presets; the quick start uses only the Sheets Core preset . Images use the corresponding drawing plugins. See the feature comparison for detailed open-source and commercial coverage.

 The demos below showcase the wider Univer Office SDK , including commercial capabilities. They show more than the default open-source setup; see open source and commercial extensions for scope.

 🚀 Build on the open-source foundation

 Your goal
 Use the open-source foundation
 Start here

 Embed Sheets or Docs
 Add an editable Office surface to your application or agent product, and connect your data through Facade APIs.
 Quick start

 Process content without an editor
 Reuse content plugins, models, commands, and calculation in Node.js for editing, snapshots, and automated tasks.
 Headless guide

 Develop custom features or editors
 Reuse the engines, UI components, plugin boundaries, dependency injection, and command/undo systems. Follow existing features to extend Sheets and Docs or develop your own editors.
 Open-source architecture

 Coordinate edits and undo/redo across features. Inserting a row inside a filter range changes both the base content and the filter range; undo needs to restore both. Each feature supplies its own changes and undo data, and the command composes their execution and history. The architecture walkthrough explains how to extend these editing workflows.

 Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor

 In a browser application using a bundler such as Vite:

 pnpm add @univerjs/presets @univerjs/preset-sheets-core

 Create the container before initializing Univer:

 < div id =" app " style =" height: 100vh " > </ div >

 import { UniverSheetsCorePreset } from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core'
 import UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/locales/en-US'
 import { createUniver , LocaleType , mergeLocales } from '@univerjs/presets'
 import '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/lib/index.css'

 const { univerAPI } = createUniver ( {
 locale : LocaleType . EN_US ,
 locales : {
 [ LocaleType . EN_US ] : mergeLocales ( UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS ) ,
 } ,
 presets : [
 UniverSheetsCorePreset ( {
 container : 'app' ,
 } ) ,
 ] ,
 } )

 univerAPI . createWorkbook ( { } )

 Your page now contains a spreadsheet editor. Use the returned univerAPI to work with its content. This example uses open-source packages and needs no commercial Univer license or Server SDK.

 For component frameworks, retain the univer instance returned by createUniver and call univer.dispose() when the component unmounts. See the lifecycle guide .

 Presets compose plugins and register their Facade APIs. For manual control, see the Plugin Mode example below. The installation guide covers both modes, peer dependencies, and framework integrations.

 Keep coordinated @univerjs/* packages on the same version. Commercial packages must use the matching release line; independently released packages such as icons follow their declared compatibility. See the API Stability Policy .

 Connect your application to editable content

 Facade APIs are the application-facing interface to workbooks, worksheets, and ranges. Continue from the quick start to populate a quotation, update a quantity from application code, and read the recalculated total:

 // Wait for formula controllers before editing a newly created workbook.
 await new Promise < void > ( ( resolve ) => {
 if ( univerAPI . getCurrentLifecycleStage ( ) >= univerAPI . Enum . LifecycleStages . Steady ) {
 resolve ( )
 return
 }
 const listener = univerAPI . addEvent ( univerAPI . Event . LifeCycleChanged , ( { stage } ) => {
 if ( stage === univerAPI . Enum . LifecycleStages . Steady ) {
 listener . dispose ( )
 resolve ( )
 }
 } )
 } )

 const workbook = univerAPI . getActiveWorkbook ( ) !
 const sheet = workbook . getActiveSheet ( )

 sheet . getRange ( 'A1:D4' ) . setValues ( [
 [ 'Item' , 'Quantity' , 'Unit price' , 'Amount' ] ,
 [ 'Seats' , 2 , 25 , '=B2*C2' ] ,
 [ 'Support' , 1 , 100 , '=B3*C3' ] ,
 [ 'Total' , '' , '' , '=SUM(D2:D3)' ] ,
 ] )

 // An application control or agent can make the same edit.
 sheet . getRange ( 'B2' ) . setValue ( 4 )

 univerAPI . getFormula ( ) . onCalculationResultApplied ( ) . then ( ( ) => {
 console . log ( sheet . getRange ( 'D4' ) . getValue ( ) ) // 200
 localStorage . setItem ( 'quotation' , JSON . stringify ( workbook . save ( ) ) )
 } ) . catch ( console . error )

 The editor and your application operate on the same workbook; formula changes are recalculated automatically. workbook.save() returns a JSON snapshot containing the workbook and its registered plugin data. Your application owns persistence; this example uses browser storage. On a later page load, after initialization, restore the snapshot instead of creating a blank workbook :

 const saved = localStorage . getItem ( 'quotation' )
 if ( saved ) {
 univerAPI . createWorkbook ( JSON . parse ( saved ) )
 }

 This workflow uses only open-source packages. Snapshot persistence is separate from XLSX import and export, which uses the separately distributed file-conversion capabilities. Use public Facade APIs for application integration; the source links below explain internal implementation and extension points. See the API Stability Policy before depending on an extension point.

 Advanced: compose plugins manually (Plugin Mode)

representativeRepos.readmeText:
The open protocol that connects any agent to any app.

 Docs · Examples · Spec · Discord

 AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.

 Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent. The same agent can power a web app, a mobile app, a terminal, or Slack.

 Important
 AG-UI 1.0 is here. The protocol now has a stable, frozen specification backed by a JSON Schema, and the TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs are generated from it. 1.0 is backwards compatible in both directions: 0.x agents work with 1.0 clients and vice versa. What changed → · Migration guide →

 Quick start

 Start a new app. The CLI scaffolds a frontend ( CopilotKit on Next.js, or a terminal client) wired to the agent framework you pick:

 npx create-ag-ui-app@latest

 Then follow the printed next steps. The generated templates call OpenAI, so set your key before npm run dev :

 export OPENAI_API_KEY= " sk-... "

 Or speak the protocol directly: a 30-line agent server and client

 An AG-UI agent is any HTTP endpoint that accepts a RunAgentInput and streams events back. No API keys needed for this one.

 1. The agent (Python). Requires Python 3.9+.

 pip install ag-ui-protocol fastapi uvicorn

 # server.py
 import uuid

 from fastapi import FastAPI , Request
 from fastapi . responses import StreamingResponse
 from ag_ui . core import (
 PROTOCOL_VERSION ,
 RunAgentInput ,
 RunStartedEvent ,
 RunFinishedEvent ,
 TextMessageStartEvent ,
 TextMessageContentEvent ,
 TextMessageEndEvent ,
)
 from ag_ui . encoder import EventEncoder

 app = FastAPI ()

 @ app . post ( "/" )
 async def run_agent ( input_data : RunAgentInput , request : Request ):
 encoder = EventEncoder ( accept = request . headers . get ( "accept" ))

 async def events ():
 yield encoder . encode ( RunStartedEvent (
 thread_id = input_data . thread_id ,
 run_id = input_data . run_id ,
 protocol_version = PROTOCOL_VERSION ,
 ))
 message_id = str ( uuid . uuid4 ())
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageStartEvent ( message_id = message_id , role = "assistant" ))
 for chunk in [ "Hello " , "from " , "AG-UI!" ]:
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageContentEvent ( message_id = message_id , delta = chunk ))
 yield encoder . encode ( TextMessageEndEvent ( message_id = message_id ))
 yield encoder . encode ( RunFinishedEvent ( thread_id = input_data . thread_id , run_id = input_data . run_id ))

 return StreamingResponse ( events (), media_type = encoder . get_content_type ())

 uvicorn server:app --port 8000

 2. The client (TypeScript). In a second terminal, in a new folder. Requires Node.js 20+.

 npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module
npm install @ag-ui/client tsx

 // client.ts
 import { HttpAgent } from "@ag-ui/client" ;

 const agent = new HttpAgent ( { url : "http://localhost:8000/" } ) ;

 agent . addMessage ( { id : crypto . randomUUID ( ) , role : "user" , content : "Hi there!" } ) ;

 await agent . runAgent ( { } , {
 onRunStartedEvent : ( { event } ) => console . log ( `run started (AG-UI ${ event . protocolVersion } )` ) ,
 onTextMessageContentEvent : ( { event } ) => { process . stdout . write ( event . delta ) ; } ,
 onRunFinishedEvent : ( ) => console . log ( "\nrun finished" ) ,
 } ) ;

 npx tsx client.ts

 You should see Hello from AG-UI! stream in. Swap the server for any supported framework and the client doesn't change.

 Where AG-UI fits

 AG-UI is one of three open, complementary agentic protocols. MCP gives agents tools and context, A2A lets agents work with other agents, and AG-UI brings agents to users. A single agent often uses all three, and AG-UI can front agents that speak MCP or A2A. Read more →

 Note
 AG-UI or A2UI? They work together. A2UI , MCP Apps, and Open-JSON-UI are generative UI specs : they describe what UI an agent wants to show. AG-UI is the runtime protocol that carries those payloads, along with everything else, between the agent and the app. Learn more →

 Integrations

 AG-UI is adopted by Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle, and built into most agent frameworks. Every framework below has a live demo in the Dojo .

 Full list of integrations

 Show all integrations

- Partners: LangChain · CrewAI

- Built in: Microsoft Agent Framework · Google ADK ( JS ) · Google Antigravity · AWS Strands Agents · Mastra · Pydantic AI · Agno · LlamaIndex · AG2

- More frameworks: Claude Agent SDK · Claude Managed Agents · IBM watsonx Orchestrate · Langroid · Spring AI · Cloudflare Agents · Omnara · Genkit (Go) · OpenAI Agents

- Specs: Oracle Agent Spec

- Deployment: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

 Source for every integration lives in integrations/ and middlewares/ , and the demos in apps/dojo .

 SDKs

 Language
 Install
 Reference

 TypeScript

 Docs · Source

 Docs · Source
